+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Exercise resolver ownership without DNS requests or unrelated processes."""
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import shlex
+import signal
+import subprocess
+import tempfile
+import time
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--source-root", type=Path, default=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1])
+    parser.add_argument("--report", type=Path)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    root = args.source_root.resolve()
+    fixture = Path(__file__).with_suffix(".c").resolve()
+    commands = []
+    report = {"source_root": str(root), "commands": commands,
+              "inputs": {str(p): hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
+                         for p in (root / "src/net.c", root / "src/net.h", fixture)},
+              "environment": {k: os.environ[k] for k in ("CC", "CFLAGS", "CPPFLAGS", "LDFLAGS", "ASAN_OPTIONS", "UBSAN_OPTIONS") if k in os.environ}}
+
+    def run(command, label):
+        started = time.monotonic()
+        process = subprocess.Popen(command, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
+                                   text=True, start_new_session=True)
+        try:
+            stdout, stderr = process.communicate(timeout=15)
+        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+            os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
+            stdout, stderr = process.communicate()
+            stderr += "\nFixture process group killed after timeout.\n"
+        commands.append({"label": label, "command": command, "returncode": process.returncode,
+                         "elapsed_seconds": time.monotonic() - started, "stdout": stdout, "stderr": stderr})
+        print(f"{label}: {'PASS' if process.returncode == 0 else 'FAIL'}", flush=True)
+        if stdout:
+            print(stdout, end="", flush=True)
+        if stderr:
+            print(stderr, end="", flush=True)
+        return process.returncode == 0
+
+    okay = False
+    try:
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="irc-resolver-ownership-") as temporary:
+            directory = Path(temporary)
+            obj, binary = directory / "net.o", directory / "resolver-ownership"
+            compiler = shlex.split(os.environ.get("CC", "cc"))
+            flags = ["-std=c11", "-O2", "-g", "-Wall", "-Wextra", "-Wpedantic", "-Werror"]
+            flags += shlex.split(os.environ.get("CPPFLAGS", "")) + shlex.split(os.environ.get("CFLAGS", ""))
+            include = ["-I", str(root / "src")]
+            renames = [f"-D{name}=resolver_ownership_{name}" for name in ("fork", "pipe", "kill", "getaddrinfo")]
+            if not run(compiler + flags + include + renames + ["-c", str(root / "src/net.c"), "-o", str(obj)], "compile resolver transport"):
+                return 1
+            if not run(compiler + flags + include + [str(fixture), str(obj)] +
+                       shlex.split(os.environ.get("LDFLAGS", "")) + ["-lssl", "-lcrypto", "-o", str(binary)], "compile resolver fixture"):
+                return 1
+            report["binary_sha256"] = hashlib.sha256(binary.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
+            okay = run([str(binary)], "resolver child ownership")
+    finally:
+        report["passed"] = okay
+        if args.report:
+            args.report.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+            args.report.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="ascii")
+    return 0 if okay else 1
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

@@ -0,0 +1,113 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Verified loopback TLS fairness, record buffering, and write retry ordering.
+
+Only the want-read case injects a TLS return value. Certificates and private
+keys are generated inside an owner-only temporary directory. No external
+network service, user configuration, or running client is accessed.
+"""
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import shlex
+import signal
+import subprocess
+import tempfile
+import time
+
+
+def digest(path):
+    return hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--source-root", type=Path, default=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1])
+    parser.add_argument("--report", type=Path)
+    parser.add_argument("--updates", type=int, default=10000)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    root = args.source_root.resolve()
+    fixture = Path(__file__).with_suffix(".c").resolve()
+    records = []
+    report = {"source_root": str(root), "fixture": str(fixture), "commands": records,
+              "inputs": {str(p): digest(p) for p in (root / "src/net.c", root / "src/net.h", fixture)},
+              "environment": {k: os.environ[k] for k in ("CC", "CFLAGS", "CPPFLAGS", "LDFLAGS", "ASAN_OPTIONS", "UBSAN_OPTIONS") if k in os.environ}}
+
+    def run(command, label, timeout=35):
+        started = time.monotonic()
+        process = subprocess.Popen(command, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
+                                   text=True, start_new_session=True)
+        try:
+            stdout, stderr = process.communicate(timeout=timeout)
+        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+            os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
+            stdout, stderr = process.communicate()
+            stderr += "\nFixture process group killed after timeout.\n"
+        result = {"label": label, "command": command, "returncode": process.returncode,
+                  "elapsed_seconds": time.monotonic() - started,
+                  "stdout": stdout, "stderr": stderr}
+        records.append(result)
+        print(f"{label}: {'PASS' if process.returncode == 0 else 'FAIL'}", flush=True)
+        if stdout:
+            print(stdout, end="", flush=True)
+        if stderr and label != "generate private loopback certificate":
+            print(stderr, end="", flush=True)
+        return process.returncode == 0
+
+    success = True
+    try:
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="irc-tls-budget-") as temporary:
+            directory = Path(temporary)
+            compiler = shlex.split(os.environ.get("CC", "cc"))
+            flags = ["-std=c11", "-O2", "-g", "-Wall", "-Wextra", "-Wpedantic", "-Werror"]
+            flags += shlex.split(os.environ.get("CPPFLAGS", ""))
+            flags += shlex.split(os.environ.get("CFLAGS", ""))
+            linker = shlex.split(os.environ.get("LDFLAGS", ""))
+            capability = directory / "capability.c"
+            capability.write_text(
+                "#include <openssl/ssl.h>\n"
+                "int main(int argc, char **argv) { (void)argv; if (argc == 12345) {\n"
+                "SSL_key_update((SSL *)0, SSL_KEY_UPDATE_NOT_REQUESTED);\n"
+                "SSL_set0_wbio((SSL *)0, (BIO *)0);\n"
+                "SSL_CTX_set_num_tickets((SSL_CTX *)0, 0);\n"
+                "SSL_has_pending((SSL *)0);\n"
+                "return SSL3_MT_KEY_UPDATE; } return 0; }\n", encoding="ascii")
+            if not run(compiler + flags + [str(capability)] + linker +
+                       ["-lssl", "-lcrypto", "-o", str(directory / "capability")],
+                       "check TLS fixture API availability"):
+                report["available"] = False
+                success = False
+                print("UNAVAILABLE: this fixture needs OpenSSL KeyUpdate and memory-BIO APIs; no TLS execution is claimed.", flush=True)
+                return 77
+            report["available"] = True
+            cert, key = directory / "cert.pem", directory / "key.pem"
+            if not run(["openssl", "req", "-x509", "-newkey", "rsa:2048", "-nodes",
+                        "-keyout", str(key), "-out", str(cert), "-days", "1",
+                        "-subj", "/CN=localhost", "-addext", "subjectAltName=DNS:localhost,IP:127.0.0.1"],
+                       "generate private loopback certificate"):
+                return 1
+            report["certificate_sha256"] = digest(cert)
+            include = ["-I", str(root / "src")]
+            renames = [f"-DSSL_{name}=tls_budget_SSL_{name}" for name in ("new", "read", "write", "get_error")]
+            obj, binary = directory / "net.o", directory / "tls-budget"
+            if not run(compiler + flags + include + renames + ["-c", str(root / "src/net.c"), "-o", str(obj)], "compile production transport"):
+                return 1
+            if not run(compiler + flags + include + [str(fixture), str(obj)] +
+                       linker + ["-lssl", "-lcrypto", "-o", str(binary)], "compile TLS fixture"):
+                return 1
+            report["binary_sha256"] = digest(binary)
+            for case in ("budget", "coalesced", "fragment", "fragment12", "truncated", "corrupt",
+                         "write-priority", "write-priority12", "want-read", "reset-write"):
+                if not run([str(binary), str(cert), str(key), case, str(args.updates)], case):
+                    success = False
+    finally:
+        report["passed"] = success and all(record["returncode"] == 0 for record in records)
+        if args.report:
+            args.report.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+            args.report.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="ascii")
+    return 0 if success else 1
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+++ vipirc-0.7.28/tests/test_net_tls_budget.py
@@ -0,0 +1,113 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Verified loopback TLS fairness, record buffering, and write retry ordering.
+
+Only the want-read case injects a TLS return value. Certificates and private
+keys are generated inside an owner-only temporary directory. No external
+network service, user configuration, or running client is accessed.
+"""
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import shlex
+import signal
+import subprocess
+import tempfile
+import time
+
+
+def digest(path):
+    return hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--source-root", type=Path, default=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1])
+    parser.add_argument("--report", type=Path)
+    parser.add_argument("--updates", type=int, default=10000)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    root = args.source_root.resolve()
+    fixture = Path(__file__).with_suffix(".c").resolve()
+    records = []
+    report = {"source_root": str(root), "fixture": str(fixture), "commands": records,
+              "inputs": {str(p): digest(p) for p in (root / "src/net.c", root / "src/net.h", fixture)},
+              "environment": {k: os.environ[k] for k in ("CC", "CFLAGS", "CPPFLAGS", "LDFLAGS", "ASAN_OPTIONS", "UBSAN_OPTIONS") if k in os.environ}}
+
+    def run(command, label, timeout=35):
+        started = time.monotonic()
+        process = subprocess.Popen(command, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
+                                   text=True, start_new_session=True)
+        try:
+            stdout, stderr = process.communicate(timeout=timeout)
+        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+            os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
+            stdout, stderr = process.communicate()
+            stderr += "\nFixture process group killed after timeout.\n"
+        result = {"label": label, "command": command, "returncode": process.returncode,
+                  "elapsed_seconds": time.monotonic() - started,
+                  "stdout": stdout, "stderr": stderr}
+        records.append(result)
+        print(f"{label}: {'PASS' if process.returncode == 0 else 'FAIL'}", flush=True)
+        if stdout:
+            print(stdout, end="", flush=True)
+        if stderr and label != "generate private loopback certificate":
+            print(stderr, end="", flush=True)
+        return process.returncode == 0
+
+    success = True
+    try:
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="irc-tls-budget-") as temporary:
+            directory = Path(temporary)
+            compiler = shlex.split(os.environ.get("CC", "cc"))
+            flags = ["-std=c11", "-O2", "-g", "-Wall", "-Wextra", "-Wpedantic", "-Werror"]
+            flags += shlex.split(os.environ.get("CPPFLAGS", ""))
+            flags += shlex.split(os.environ.get("CFLAGS", ""))
+            linker = shlex.split(os.environ.get("LDFLAGS", ""))
+            capability = directory / "capability.c"
+            capability.write_text(
+                "#include <openssl/ssl.h>\n"
+                "int main(int argc, char **argv) { (void)argv; if (argc == 12345) {\n"
+                "SSL_key_update((SSL *)0, SSL_KEY_UPDATE_NOT_REQUESTED);\n"
+                "SSL_set0_wbio((SSL *)0, (BIO *)0);\n"
+                "SSL_CTX_set_num_tickets((SSL_CTX *)0, 0);\n"
+                "SSL_has_pending((SSL *)0);\n"
+                "return SSL3_MT_KEY_UPDATE; } return 0; }\n", encoding="ascii")
+            if not run(compiler + flags + [str(capability)] + linker +
+                       ["-lssl", "-lcrypto", "-o", str(directory / "capability")],
+                       "check TLS fixture API availability"):
+                report["available"] = False
+                success = False
+                print("UNAVAILABLE: this fixture needs OpenSSL KeyUpdate and memory-BIO APIs; no TLS execution is claimed.", flush=True)
+                return 77
+            report["available"] = True
+            cert, key = directory / "cert.pem", directory / "key.pem"
+            if not run(["openssl", "req", "-x509", "-newkey", "rsa:2048", "-nodes",
+                        "-keyout", str(key), "-out", str(cert), "-days", "1",
+                        "-subj", "/CN=localhost", "-addext", "subjectAltName=DNS:localhost,IP:127.0.0.1"],
+                       "generate private loopback certificate"):
+                return 1
+            report["certificate_sha256"] = digest(cert)
+            include = ["-I", str(root / "src")]
+            renames = [f"-DSSL_{name}=tls_budget_SSL_{name}" for name in ("new", "read", "write", "get_error")]
+            obj, binary = directory / "net.o", directory / "tls-budget"
+            if not run(compiler + flags + include + renames + ["-c", str(root / "src/net.c"), "-o", str(obj)], "compile production transport"):
+                return 1
+            if not run(compiler + flags + include + [str(fixture), str(obj)] +
+                       linker + ["-lssl", "-lcrypto", "-o", str(binary)], "compile TLS fixture"):
+                return 1
+            report["binary_sha256"] = digest(binary)
+            for case in ("budget", "coalesced", "fragment", "fragment12", "truncated", "corrupt",
+                         "write-priority", "write-priority12", "want-read", "reset-write"):
+                if not run([str(binary), str(cert), str(key), case, str(args.updates)], case):
+                    success = False
+    finally:
+        report["passed"] = success and all(record["returncode"] == 0 for record in records)
+        if args.report:
+            args.report.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+            args.report.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="ascii")
+    return 0 if success else 1
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Assemble exact current evidence and retain clearly scoped development records."""
import difflib
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
from run_deep import inputs as current_inputs

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
OUT = ROOT/"irc-deep-validation"
WORK = ROOT/"irc-deep-work"
BASE = ROOT/"irc-deep-baseline"
PAIRS = (("onekeyirc-0.1.26", "onekeyirc-0.1.27"), ("vipirc-0.7.27", "vipirc-0.7.28"))
REPORT = "SECURITY-DEEP-REVIEW-2026-11-16.txt"
RESULTS = "DEEP-TEST-RESULTS.json"


def sha(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def read(path):
    return json.loads(path.read_text())


required = ["release-configure", "release-strict-build", "release-one-sanitize-build",
            "release-vip-idle-normal-build", "release-vip-idle-sanitize-build",
            "release-security-normal", "release-efficiency-normal", "release-session-controls-normal",
            "release-detach-normal", "release-compat-units-build", "release-test_app",
            "release-test_credentials", "release-native-session-probe", "release-security-sanitize",
            "release-session-controls-sanitize", "release-one-sanitize-availability",
            "release-vip-deep-normal", "release-vip-deep-sanitize"]
required += ["release-" + name for name in ("cli", "commands", "setup-async", "setup-paths",
              "autojoin-reconnect", "wrapping", "notice", "terminal-policy")]
required += ["release-vip-idle-" + label + "-" + name for label in ("normal", "sanitize")
             for name in ("cli", "commands", "wrapping", "availability", "notice", "terminal-policy")]
history = read(OUT/"deep-gates.json")
latest = {r["name"]: r for r in history}
assert len(required) == len(set(required))
assert set(required) <= latest.keys(), sorted(set(required)-latest.keys())
for name in required:
    allowed = ("PASS", "UNAVAILABLE") if name == "release-native-session-probe" else ("PASS",)
    assert latest[name]["status"] in allowed, (name, latest[name])
gates = [latest[name] for name in required]
frozen_inputs = current_inputs()
for gate in gates:
    assert gate["inputs_before"] == frozen_inputs and gate["inputs_after"] == frozen_inputs, gate["name"]

static_history = read(OUT/"static/results.json")
static = list({r["source"]: r for r in static_history}.values())
assert len(static) == 3
for r in static:
    assert sha(ROOT/r["source"]) == r["sha256"], r["source"]
    assert read(OUT/"static"/r["log"]) == r["diagnostics"]
    if r["source"].endswith("/net.c"):
        assert r["exit_code"] == 1 and len(r["diagnostics"]) == 1
        assert r["diagnostics"][0]["option"] == "-Werror=analyzer-fd-leak"
        assert (OUT/"local/static-triage/TRIAGE.txt").is_file()
        r["review_disposition"] = "TRIAGED_FALSE_POSITIVE_WITH_BASELINE_AND_MINIMAL_CONTROLS"
    else:
        assert r["exit_code"] == 0 and r["diagnostics"] == []
        r["review_disposition"] = "NO_DIAGNOSTIC"

common = sorted({p.name for p in (WORK/PAIRS[0][1]/"src").iterdir() if p.is_file()} &
                {p.name for p in (WORK/PAIRS[1][1]/"src").iterdir() if p.is_file()})
assert len(common) == 38
for name in common:
    assert (WORK/PAIRS[0][1]/"src"/name).read_bytes() == (WORK/PAIRS[1][1]/"src"/name).read_bytes(), name
binary_hashes = read(OUT/"final-binary-hashes.json")
for path, expected in binary_hashes.items():
    assert sha(ROOT/path) == expected, path
packaging = read(OUT/"packaging-validation.json")
assert packaging["status"] == "PASS" and packaging["identical_tested_binary"]

# Final agent records retain their own expected vulnerable-baseline outcomes.
network = read(OUT/"network/final-command-results.json")
assert network["matched_all_expected_outcomes"]
for path, expected in network["candidate_source_sha256"].items():
    assert sha(Path(path)) == expected, path
for record in network["commands"]:
    assert record["matched_expected_outcome"], record["label"]
assert "validation_correction" in network
local = read(OUT/"local/local-checks.json")
assert all(r["compile_exit"] == 0 and r["run_exit"] == 0 for r in local)
for r in read(OUT/"local/source-hashes.json"):
    project = PAIRS[0][1] if r["app"] == "onekeyirc" else PAIRS[1][1]
    assert sha(WORK/project/r["path"]) == r["sha256"], r
state = read(OUT/"state/release-results.json")
for r in state:
    assert not r["source_changed_during_validation"]
    for path, expected in r["source_sha256"].items():
        assert sha(Path(path)) == expected, (r["label"], path)
    for step in r["steps"]:
        # The state runner records compile and execution as separate steps.
        code = step.get("returncode", step.get("exit_code"))
        assert code == 0, (r["label"], step)

source_hashes, changes = {}, {}
for old, new in PAIRS:
    tree = WORK/new
    source_hashes[new] = {str(p.relative_to(tree)): sha(p) for area in ("src", "tests")
                          for p in sorted((tree/area).iterdir()) if p.is_file() and p.suffix in (".c", ".h", ".py")}
    changes[new] = {}
    for area in ("src", "tests"):
        for path in sorted((tree/area).iterdir()):
            if not path.is_file() or path.suffix not in (".c", ".h", ".py"):
                continue
            rel = path.relative_to(tree)
            before = BASE/old/rel
            old_text = before.read_text() if before.exists() else ""
            if old_text != path.read_text():
                changes[new][str(rel)] = "".join(difflib.unified_diff(
                    old_text.splitlines(keepends=True), path.read_text().splitlines(keepends=True),
                    fromfile=old+"/"+str(rel), tofile=new+"/"+str(rel)))

evidence = {}
for path in sorted(OUT.rglob("*")):
    if not path.is_file() or path.suffix not in (".json", ".log", ".txt", ".c", ".py", ".diff", ".patch"):
        continue
    rel = path.relative_to(OUT)
    if len(rel.parts) > 1 and rel.parts[0] not in ("network", "local", "state", "static"):
        continue
    if path.name in ("report-body.txt", "release-integrity.json") or path.stat().st_size > 2_000_000:
        continue
    if "__pycache__" in rel.parts:
        continue
    evidence[str(rel)] = dict(sha256=sha(path), size_bytes=path.stat().st_size,
                             contents=path.read_text(errors="replace"))

summary = dict(passed_integrated_gate_groups=sum(g["status"] == "PASS" for g in gates),
               unavailable_integrated_gate_groups=sum(g["status"] == "UNAVAILABLE" for g in gates),
               failed_final_runtime_build_gate_groups=0,
               static_translation_units=3, static_units_without_diagnostics=2,
               static_diagnostics_triaged_false_positive=1,
               identical_common_source_files=len(common))
result = dict(schema_version=1, date_utc="2026-11-16", releases=[new for old, new in PAIRS],
              baselines=[old for old, new in PAIRS],
              status="EXECUTED_RUNTIME_GATES_PASS_WITH_EXPLICIT_UNAVAILABLE_SCOPE_AND_TRIAGED_STATIC_DIAGNOSTIC",
              summary=summary, final_integrated_gates=gates, all_integrated_attempts=history,
              source_hashes=source_hashes, shared_source_parity=common,
              tested_binary_hashes=binary_hashes, packaging_validation=packaging,
              static_analysis=static, static_analysis_history=static_history,
              environment=read(OUT/"environment.json"),
              final_network_records=network, final_local_records=local, final_state_records=state,
              development_evidence_note="Expected baseline failures, intermediate revisions, explicitly superseded normal/sanitizer labels and fixture corrections are preserved. Final records and hashes define the delivered source.",
              source_changes=changes, evidence_documents=evidence)

header = f"""SECURITY, EFFICIENCY AND STABILITY CONTINUATION
Date: 2026-11-16 UTC
Releases: onekeyirc 0.1.27 and vipirc 0.7.28
Baselines: onekeyirc 0.1.26 and vipirc 0.7.27

RESULT AND SCOPE

This additional source review produced shared-core security and stability
fixes, reproducible baseline failures, independent cross-reviews, corrected
sanitizer harnesses and new regression targets in both source packages.
No new authentication bypass or remote code execution was demonstrated.
This is bounded verification with explicit limits, not a certification.

Integrated final build/runtime gate groups: {summary['passed_integrated_gate_groups']} PASS,
{summary['unavailable_integrated_gate_groups']} UNAVAILABLE, 0 final runtime/build FAIL.
A group may contain multiple binaries or individual cases. The named-session
runtime probe is unavailable because native AF_UNIX bind is restricted.

Static analysis: 3 changed shared translation units reviewed; 2 emitted no
diagnostics and 1 emitted a demonstrated pre-existing analyzer false positive.
Its strict command remains exit 1 and its raw diagnostic is retained.
No wholly clean static-analysis result is claimed.

All {len(common)} common source files are identical in the two packages. A clean
standalone source build matches the tested onekeyirc binary exactly. Private
DESTDIR installation/uninstallation checks validate content and permissions;
the final archive step rechecks finalized documents and every archived byte.

The full machine-readable record is doc/DEEP-TEST-RESULTS.json in each archive.
It embeds the commands, outputs, source hashes, diffs, historical reproductions
and the separately scoped transport/local/state evidence described below.
The archive SOURCE-MANIFEST.json and SHA256SUMS verify the distributed files.

"""
body = (OUT/"report-body.txt").read_text()
table = "\nFINAL INTEGRATED GATE RECORDS\n\n"
for g in gates:
    table += g["status"] + "  " + g["name"] + "  exit=" + str(g["exit_code"]) + "  seconds=" + str(g["seconds"]) + "\n"
report = header + body + table
assert report.isascii()
encoded = json.dumps(result, indent=2, ensure_ascii=True) + "\n"
for old, new in PAIRS:
    (WORK/new/"doc"/REPORT).write_text(report)
    (WORK/new/"doc"/RESULTS).write_text(encoded)
    (WORK/new/"doc/VALIDATION.txt").write_text(
        "CURRENT SOURCE REVIEW AND VALIDATION\nonekeyirc 0.1.27 / vipirc 0.7.28\n2026-11-16 UTC\n\n"
        "See " + REPORT + " and " + RESULTS + " for the current scope.\n"
        + str(summary['passed_integrated_gate_groups']) + " integrated gate groups passed; "
        + str(summary['unavailable_integrated_gate_groups']) + " unavailable; no final runtime/build failure.\n"
        "One static-analysis warning remains documented as a demonstrated false positive.\n"
        "Full ncurses, native OpenBSD, named AF_UNIX lifecycle, real GnuPG and leak-scanning\n"
        "coverage remain explicitly limited. Historical reports apply to their named versions.\n")
(OUT/"final-summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2)+"\n")
print(json.dumps(dict(summary=summary, report_words=len(report.split()), evidence_bytes=len(encoded))))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Add the bounded continuation regressions to both source packages."""
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
NAMES = ("presence_cancellation", "presence_recovery", "credential_descendants",
         "credential_signals", "background_rights")
for name in ("onekeyirc-0.1.27", "vipirc-0.7.28"):
    folder = ROOT/"irc-deep-work"/name
    path = folder/"Makefile.in"
    text = path.read_text()
    assert "DEEP_BINS =" not in text
    stamp = "build/.stamp" if name.startswith("onekeyirc") else "build"
    bins = " ".join("build/test_" + item for item in NAMES)
    block = "\n# Bounded TLS, child ownership, presence and native descriptor regressions.\n"
    block += "DEEP_BINS = " + bins + "\n"
    block += "check-unit: check-deep\ncheck-security: check-deep\n"
    block += "check-security-sanitize: check-deep-sanitize\n\n"
    for item in NAMES:
        source = "tests/test_" + item + ".c"
        if item.startswith("presence_"):
            linked = "src/app.c src/autocommands.c src/sim.c src/protocol.c"
            dependencies = "tests/test_app.c " + linked
        elif item.startswith("credential_"):
            linked = "src/config.c src/autocommands.c src/protocol.c"
            dependencies = "tests/test_credentials.c src/credentials.c " + linked
        else:
            linked = ""
            dependencies = "src/background.c"
        block += "build/test_" + item + ": " + source + " " + dependencies + " $(HEADERS) " + stamp + "\n"
        block += "\t$(CC) $(CPPFLAGS) $(CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) -Isrc -Itests -o $@ " + source + " " + linked + "\n\n"
    block += "check-deep: $(DEEP_BINS)\n"
    for item in NAMES:
        block += "\t./build/test_" + item + "\n"
    # Exit 77 means the test's development-library capability is unavailable.
    # Preserve that visible status while allowing other portable checks to run.
    for script in ("test_net_tls_budget.py", "test_net_resolver_ownership.py"):
        block += '\tCC="$(CC)" CPPFLAGS="$(CPPFLAGS)" CFLAGS="$(CFLAGS)" LDFLAGS="$(LDFLAGS)" $(PYTHON) tests/' + script
        block += "; result=$$?; test $$result -eq 0 -o $$result -eq 77\n" if script == "test_net_tls_budget.py" else "\n"
    block += "\ncheck-deep-sanitize: " + stamp + "\n\tmkdir -p build/deep-sanitize\n"
    for item in NAMES:
        linked = ("src/app.c src/autocommands.c src/sim.c src/protocol.c" if item.startswith("presence_") else
                  "src/config.c src/autocommands.c src/protocol.c" if item.startswith("credential_") else "")
        block += "\t$(CC) $(CPPFLAGS) $(SANFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) -Isrc -Itests -o build/deep-sanitize/test_" + item
        block += " tests/test_" + item + ".c " + linked + "\n"
    for item in NAMES:
        block += "\t./build/deep-sanitize/test_" + item + "\n"
    for script in ("test_net_tls_budget.py", "test_net_resolver_ownership.py"):
        block += '\tCC="$(CC)" CPPFLAGS="$(CPPFLAGS)" CFLAGS="$(SANFLAGS)" LDFLAGS="$(LDFLAGS) -fsanitize=address,undefined" $(PYTHON) tests/' + script
        block += "; result=$$?; test $$result -eq 0 -o $$result -eq 77\n" if script == "test_net_tls_budget.py" else "\n"
    clean = "\trm -f $(DEEP_BINS) " + " ".join("build/deep-sanitize/test_" + item for item in NAMES) + "\n"
    assert text.count("\nclean:\n") == 1
    text = text.replace("\nclean:\n", "\nclean:\n" + clean)
    path.write_text(text + block)
    print("Integrated new regression targets in " + name)

local/LOCAL-REVIEW.txt.contents:
LOCAL TRUST-BOUNDARY AND HELPER LIFECYCLE FOLLOW-UP
Date: 2026-11-16

Reviewed baselines: onekeyirc 0.1.26 and vipirc 0.7.27.
Editable candidates: onekeyirc 0.1.27 and vipirc 0.7.28.
Production changes in this review: credentials.c only, identically in both
clients. Configuration, client and background production files are unchanged.

1. CONFIRMED: HELPER EXIT BEFORE INHERITED PIPE EOF LOST GROUP OWNERSHIP

The direct GPG helper was reaped as soon as it exited. Its job then retained
exited=1 while a same-process-group descendant could still hold stdout or
status open. Timeout followed by cancellation skipped group termination
because the direct helper was already marked exited. A private adversarial
helper reproduced this for both decryption and encryption; the descendant
remained alive and credential_cleanup_pending() reported zero.

Evidence: helper-baseline.txt is the initial real-process reproduction;
descendants-baseline.txt is the final regression failing against baseline.
Both probes clean up their own descendants, including on failure.

Fix: poll no longer reaps the direct helper before both result/status pipes
reach EOF. Its unreaped leader remains the ownership anchor for the numeric
process-group ID, allowing cancel/timeout to kill that owned group before
reaping. No previously reaped PID is saved and signalled later. Normal pipe
EOF still permits exit collection and slot reuse.

Scope: this is a real local helper availability/cleanup defect. It is not a
demonstration that a remote IRC peer can execute a helper or spawn a process.
The executable, same-UID processes and root remain trusted. This mechanism
is not a subprocess sandbox; a deliberately escaping helper is outside the
guarantee. The clients do not install an independent child-reaping handler.

New test: tests/test_credential_descendants.c. Real fork/exec/pipes/signals,
with this test executable as the helper, never a real GPG keyring. Both
decrypt/encrypt cover stdout-only, status-only and both inherited writers;
explicit cancel and timeout; malformed status failure; a leader exiting
before 1000 buffered bytes finish draining under one-byte reads; normal EOF
releasing the slot; descriptor restoration. On Linux, test-only subreaping
collects every descendant created by the fixture.

2. CONFIRMED ADMISSION GAP: AUTOMATIC SIGCHLD REAPING

Baseline helper startup accepted SIGCHLD=SIG_IGN and SA_NOCLDWAIT. Those
policies invalidate the unreaped-child ownership assumption on platforms or
launch contexts where they are retained. The new guard queries sigaction
before launching either kind of helper and rejects those policies with an
actionable SIGCHLD diagnostic, without opening credential pipes or forking.
SIG_DFL and a non-reaping handler continue to work. No global signal policy
or terminal interrupt/suspend character is changed.

Evidence: signals-baseline.txt records actual forks under the rejected
policies. The final tests prove zero forks, restored descriptors and no
published destination for rejected policies, and normal startup otherwise.
All test signal dispositions are restored before completion.

Platform scope: execution here is Linux. OpenBSD sigaction(2) documents that
execve resets SIGCHLD; this finding must not imply that an ordinary OpenBSD
exec preserves ignored SIGCHLD. The guard still checks the actual runtime
disposition portably. The root review owns the external primary citation.

New test: tests/test_credential_signals.c, using real helper process startup
and the existing adversarial helper fixture. A fork wrapper only counts
attempts. There is no real GPG-agent integration claim.

3. NATIVE SCM_RIGHTS / CONTROL DECODER COVERAGE ADDED, NO NEW DEFECT FOUND

Native AF_UNIX bind was re-probed exactly once and failed with EPERM (1).
Native AF_UNIX socketpair was available. See capabilities.json. No bypass
or replacement pathname listener was used.

New test: tests/test_background_rights.c. It calls the actual background
decoder through real socketpair, sendmsg, recvmsg and SCM_RIGHTS, with real
PTY descriptors for successful attachment. Only net/credential readiness
and the monotonic-clock function are supplied by small test stubs. There
are no socket/recvmsg wrappers.

It covers 41 descriptor-count cases (0 through 40), including actual kernel
ancillary truncation; six partial-request EOF/timeout cleanups; all 287
modern query split points; unexpected rights on control queries; Linux
SCM_CREDENTIALS rejection when SO_PASSCRED is available; native same-UID
peer checks; wrong-token rejection; fragmented valid real-TTY attachment;
completion and descriptor counts. Baseline and candidates pass.
Descriptor accounting uses live F_GETFD checks for fd 0 through 1023, with
fixture-owned source/control/PTY/saved descriptors checked within that range;
it does not infer live descriptors from possibly static /dev/fd entries.

This does not execute pathname bind/listen/connect, complete CLI resume,
or an interactive ncurses frontend. The old native-session gate remains
unavailable in this environment.

4. CONFIGURATION POST-RENAME FSYNC CONCERN CLOSED AS PARTIAL COMMIT SEMANTICS

The focused storage probe uses real private files and injects one EIO from
fsync. A file fsync error before rename keeps the old file and old runtime
seed. A directory fsync error after rename returns failure with the explicit
diagnostic 'Configuration was replaced but directory synchronization failed';
the new file is present, while the caller retains the old runtime seed.
Retry succeeds and aligns the runtime with the saved file. This is an
explicit partial-commit/durability limitation, not a newly demonstrated
silent success or permission bypass. No configuration/client API behavior
was broadened in this pass.

Evidence: probe_config_commit.c and config-commit-baseline.txt. It uses
placeholder endpoints, no secrets and no network connection. An fsync fault
is a deliberate boundary injection, not a claim that the host disk failed.

5. FRONTEND ENCRYPTION / FIRST BACKGROUND FORK REVIEW

Root checked that idle SETUP consumes input, Escape cancels pending
credential creation through idle_setup_back, and finish_setup frees setup
before returning to WATCH/background. Full UI handle_key routes guided
input before command/category dispatch. return_to_chat closes guided state
before setting background_requested.

This reviewer independently checked the mouse branch: guided_active routes
to guided_mouse, calls guided_changed, and returns before status/App actions.
The App Background path calls return_to_chat before setting the request.
No reachable first background fork with a live creation job was established.
The existing readiness guard covers outstanding cancellation/reaping. No
extra broad background guard was added without a reproduction.

6. VALIDATION AND REPRODUCTION

run_local_checks.py records exact compile commands and run exit codes in
local-checks.json. All 16 current compile/run pairs pass: three new suites
in normal and ASan+UBSan modes for both clients; existing credentials and
credential_lifecycle suites normally for both clients. All compilations use
-Wall -Wextra -Werror. LeakSanitizer is disabled with detect_leaks=0 because
of the documented environment limitation; no LSan coverage is claimed.

The descendant and signal regressions fail cleanly on the baseline; the
native rights suite passes baseline and candidates. Source hashes and the
production diff are captured next to this report. Root owns final broad
integration tests, versioning, release documentation and artifact delivery.

Preserved: inherited terminal signal policy, default-off force setting,
once-per-session notice, non-destructive detach and destructive explicit
close semantics. No public IRC, live user service, real keyring, or external
message was used or modified in this review.

local/NET-CROSS-REVIEW.txt.contents:
INDEPENDENT READ-ONLY NETWORK DIFF REVIEW
Date: 2026-11-16

Scope: net.c/net.h versus onekeyirc 0.1.26 baseline, and the corresponding
app.c queue/poll/close call sites in the candidate. Both clients have shared
transport changes. No network production/test files were edited by this
reviewer; no duplicate TLS tests were run. The network owner owns execution
evidence and primary TLS-library documentation checks.

Result: no concrete integration blocker found in the reviewed change.

Pending-write ownership:
- write_output retains its OutLine and does not advance offset on -2.
- The bytes and remaining length passed to SSL_write therefore remain
  unchanged across retry. Only positive progress changes offset.
- Queue cancellation and DCC-offer cancellation retain the in-flight frame.
- app_events requests output while inflight exists. It cannot legitimately
  discard that frame yet keep a READY Net waiting for a write retry.
- app_request_quit clears queues only when there is no in-flight frame.
- app_disconnect and app_free close the transport/SSL object before freeing
  the in-flight frame, preserving its lifetime through SSL cleanup.

Poll/read suppression:
- The same write_retry && write_want == POLLOUT predicate controls
  net_events, net_read and net_pending. A stalled SSL_write therefore does
  not cause decoded read bytes to force zero-timeout work or another read.
- app_timeout returns a bounded normal timeout when inflight is present;
  it cannot fall through to an expired queued-chat timer in that state.
- Positive SSL_write progress clears write_retry. WANT_READ remains eligible
  for input and is deliberately not treated like WANT_WRITE.
- Terminal failure moves to NET_FAILED, gating subsequent I/O/events;
  reconnect allocates a fresh zero-initialized Net, so retry state is not
  inherited by a new TLS connection. net_close frees the pending SSL state.

TLS control-record yielding:
- AUTO_RETRY is cleared and read-ahead is disabled only on the per-connection
  SSL object backed by the direct socket BIO. The existing verification,
  identity checks and TLS minimum are unchanged by the diff.
- Existing per-turn application read/write budgets remain in place.
- The network owner's real loopback TLS/control-record, partial-record,
  write-backpressure and failure tests are the runtime evidence; this review
  adds call-site/lifetime checking, not an additional runtime claim.

Resolver SIGCHLD guard:
- SIG_IGN/SA_NOCLDWAIT and sigaction-query failure reject before resolver
  pipe/fork. net_open rollback still has resolver=0 and fd=-1 on this path;
  TLS context allocation, if present, is freed by the normal close path.
- The failure is nonretryable, preventing an automatic launch retry loop.
- The source/header contract excludes external reaping or policy changes
  while a resolver is owned. The app does not install a separate reaper.
- This is an inherited-policy safety condition, not a remote exploit.

Residual scope: no forced PID reuse, no malicious same-UID process or helper
sandboxing, and no native OpenBSD execution were claimed by this review.

local/static-triage/TRIAGE.txt.contents:
GCC 14.2 ANALYZER FD-LEAK TRIAGE
Date: 2026-11-16

Conclusion: the diagnostic at resolver_isolate's dup2(*result_fd, 3) is a
confirmed analyzer false positive in this case. It is pre-existing in both
baselines, not introduced by the candidate transport changes. No production
code was edited and no warning was suppressed. The strict analyzer invocation
still returns exit 1, and its raw diagnostic is preserved.

1. Exact comparison

The command is copied from root's static/results.json with only the source
and output paths adjusted. Each compilation runs in its project directory
so -Isrc has the same meaning. All flags, including -O0, -fanalyzer, -Werror,
-Wformat=2, -Werror=format-security, feature macros and -DONEKEY_ONLY, remain
unchanged for this comparison.

onekeyirc 0.1.26 baseline: analyzer-fd-leak, exit 1, net.c line 226.
onekeyirc 0.1.27 candidate: analyzer-fd-leak, exit 1, net.c line 227.
vipirc 0.7.27 baseline: analyzer-fd-leak, exit 1, net.c line 226.
vipirc 0.7.28 candidate: analyzer-fd-leak, exit 1, net.c line 227.

The diagnostic says the descriptor returned by dup2 leaks at the same
conditional expression that checks for failure. The resolver_isolate body
is identical across these snapshots. comparison.json retains exact commands,
source hashes, locations and diagnostic tails; individual JSON files retain
the complete analyzer paths. compiler.txt records the compiler version.

2. Discriminating minimal cases

All use the same exact analyzer flags:

minimal-literal-close.c:
  if (dup2(source, 3) < 0) return -1;
  close(3);
  return 0;
This correct duplicate-and-close function produces the same fd-leak warning.

minimal-return-close.c:
  int copy = dup2(source, 3);
  if (copy < 0) return -1;
  close(copy);
  return 0;
This semantically equivalent function is analyzer-clean.

minimal-checked-literal.c records the return, checks it equals 3, and closes
the literal descriptor 3. It is also clean. The analyzer is failing to carry
the successful dup2 return-value identity into the known target descriptor.

minimal-real-leak.c omits the close and warns, retained as a positive control.
minimal-results.json and the per-case raw JSON preserve every outcome.

3. Actual descriptor ownership and failure paths

dup2(old, 3) has a specified target descriptor. Successful completion returns
3, replacing any prior target reference as part of the operation. It does
not allocate an unrelated descriptor number that is lost when the return is
used only as a condition. Failure returns -1; the caller still has its source
descriptor. OpenBSD's primary manual documents these return/target semantics
and the EBADF, EBUSY, EINTR and EIO errors.

The resolver is already a forked child when resolver_isolate executes:

- If the result descriptor already equals 3, no duplication occurs.
- After successful dup2, *result_fd becomes 3. The original source is among
  descriptors 0..2 or 4 and above and is closed by the ensuing isolation.
- A dup2 failure leaves *result_fd pointing at the original result pipe.
  resolver_isolate returns failure to resolve_child, which sends a bounded
  failure result through that descriptor, closes it and calls _exit.
- A later isolation failure has already recorded target 3. resolve_child's
  same send_result path closes 3 and exits. Any other child-only inherited
  descriptors still present on a failed isolation path close at process exit;
  failed isolation never proceeds into getaddrinfo.
- Successful isolation deliberately retains fd 3 while the lookup runs.
  The completed result is written, fd 3 is explicitly closed, and the child
  exits. Parent cancellation/deadline terminates and collects a stuck helper.

The parent and child have separate descriptor tables after fork. The child
duplication does not create an additional leaked descriptor in the parent.

4. Existing runtime evidence

tests/test_net.py resolver_isolation executes production net.c with a
getaddrinfo fixture that examines live descriptors after isolation. It checks
that fd 3 is a close-on-exec pipe, that 0..2 and 4..31 are closed, and that a
previously open high descriptor above a lowered RLIMIT_NOFILE is closed.
The parent separately checks EOF on unrelated socket/pipe pairs while the
lookup remains blocked, plus cancellation/deadline child collection.

Its Linux variants exercise native close_range, a forced ENOSYS fallback to
real fd-table enumeration, and unavailable enumeration that must fail closed
without entering lookup. Network-owner final-command-results.json and
retained-test_net-normal.log record a passing normal run. These observations
support the ownership analysis; they are not a proof of every possible OS
failure or a replacement for reviewing the warning itself.

Validation-label correction discovered during this review: test_net.py does
not consume CFLAGS/LDFLAGS. An earlier network record named retained-test_net-
sanitize changed only those environment variables, so it did not instrument
that retained test. Root and network owner were notified to correct the
label or rerun through the supported CC setting with explicit sanitizer
flags. This triage relies on its normal execution only. New dedicated TLS
and resolver-ownership sanitizer suites are separate evidence.

5. Primary references

OpenBSD dup(2), including dup2 target and return semantics:
https://man.openbsd.org/dup2.2

GCC 14.2 Static Analyzer Options, describing fd-leak diagnostics and stating
that the analyzer may produce false positives and false negatives:
https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc-14.2.0/gcc/Static-Analyzer-Options.html

The current Open Group page returned HTTP 403 to retrieval; no assertion in
this triage depends on having read that inaccessible page. This report does
not label the overall static-analysis gate clean: the diagnostic remains
present, with the concrete reason it does not represent a runtime leak here.

network/final-findings.txt.contents:
TRANSPORT SECURITY AND STABILITY FOLLOW-UP
Date: 2026-11-16 UTC
Baseline: onekeyirc 0.1.26 / vipirc 0.7.27
Candidate source directories: onekeyirc 0.1.27 / vipirc 0.7.28

SCOPE AND RESULT

This agent changed src/net.c, src/net.h, four new transport test files, and
the two retained Python transport harnesses to honor their build flags.
Both candidate copies match byte for byte. No app.c, protocol.c, config.c,
background.c, Makefile or release-version edits were made by this agent.
No public IRC connection, live user worker, account configuration or installed
client was accessed. Network execution used only private loopback TLS/TCP.
The generated test certificate is explicitly trusted only by its test client;
IP identity and peer verification stay enabled throughout.

Sixteen final candidate command gates passed: the two new gates and both
retained transport/retry suites in both clients, normally and under ASan/UBSan.
Two separate baseline command gates failed as expected and remain labeled
baseline defects. Source hashes stayed unchanged within each validation batch;
the retained test-harness correction and rerun are recorded explicitly below.

1. CONFIRMED AVAILABILITY DEFECT: TLS CONTROL RECORDS BYPASS READ BUDGET

With OpenSSL's default SSL_MODE_AUTO_RETRY, a single nonblocking SSL_read can
consume a long sequence of TLS 1.3 control records internally before returning
the next IRC byte. The caller's finite application-read budget does not apply
inside that call. A private, verified TLS server sent 100,000 valid KeyUpdate
records followed by a complete 22-byte PING. On the untouched baseline all
100,000 updates were processed by one net_read call. This was a real library
path, observed with its message callback; no TLS result was synthesized.

Final sequential diagnostic measurements:
  Baseline: 1 read, 100,000 updates/read, 1,203,061 us in that read.
  Candidate: 100,001 reads, at most 1 update/read, first read 603 us.
  Candidate maximum observed individual read: 4,161 us.
  Baseline 10 ms fixture timer: 1 callback, maximum lateness 1,193,071 us.
  Candidate timer: 137 callbacks, maximum lateness 2,185 us.
  Both sides completed a byte-exact PING/PONG exchange.

These timings depend on scheduling and instrumentation. They are diagnostic
observations, not real-time limits or a production-throughput benchmark. The
fixture exercises the transport with a simple event loop and 10 ms callbacks;
it does not claim to execute the actual terminal application during this run.
A single hostile server read can delay all other work in the real caller, so
returning control between records repairs the availability boundary.

The candidate clears AUTO_RETRY and explicitly disables TLS read-ahead on its
direct socket BIO. Complete unprocessed records remain readable on the socket
for the next poll. Decoded application remainders continue to be reported by
SSL_pending. It does not use SSL_has_pending to force an immediate retry:
that function also reports incomplete encrypted records.

New direct checks cover:
  - Coalesced KeyUpdate plus PING: return after the control record, then deliver
    PING on the still-readable descriptor without requiring more server bytes.
  - Actual partial TLS records: SSL_has_pending=1, net_pending=0, about 80 ms
    elapsed in a requested 80 ms poll, no premature application bytes.
  - Complete decoded TLS 1.2 and 1.3 remainders: drain without a fresh socket
    event, with byte-exact integrity across 73-byte reads.
  - Truncated ciphertext: no partial plaintext returned; transient EOF policy.
  - Corrupted ciphertext: no plaintext returned; fatal protocol error held.

Threat boundary: valid authenticated TLS control records are generated by the
TLS endpoint. This finding requires a malicious or compromised server/endpoint;
ordinary channel users or unauthenticated network attackers cannot directly
forge these records. It bounds per-call work and improves event-loop fairness;
it does not eliminate CPU/bandwidth costs under sustained hostile traffic.

Evidence: final-baseline-tls.json, final-one-tls-normal.json,
final-vip-tls-normal.json and final-*-tls_budget-sanitize.json.

2. CONFIRMED API-CONTRACT DEFECT: SSL_WRITE WANT_WRITE PRECEDENCE

OpenSSL documents that a write returning WANT_WRITE must be retried before
other TLS I/O. The application's retained in-flight IRC frame already preserves
its bytes and length correctly, but net_read previously entered SSL_read while
the preceding SSL_write still needed socket output. It also advertised
readability and decoded pending bytes during that wait. This violated the TLS
API ordering and could cause zero-time/readable wakeups that cannot help the
required write. No crash or application-byte corruption is claimed: the tested
OpenSSL 3.5.7 baseline happened to complete the stream despite the violation.

The candidate tracks a pending write retry. While it requires POLLOUT,
net_read yields without calling SSL_read, net_pending returns zero even if
OpenSSL retains decoded bytes, and net_events requests only POLLOUT. This
preserves the application's existing stable in-flight bytes until progress.
When the write succeeds, normal reads/pending bytes resume. If it instead
requires POLLIN, reads remain allowed and decoded data remains eligible.

Real TLS 1.2 and 1.3 socket-backpressure cases leave 8,191 decrypted bytes
internally pending. Baseline exposes those bytes and performs another read
while the write is stalled. Candidate suppresses that read and polls output
only, then delivers all 8,194 incoming bytes (original data plus acknowledgement)
and all 81,920 outgoing bytes exactly. A real reset during the stalled write
fails promptly with the retained transient reconnect classification.

The rare write-WANT_READ transition is explicitly fault-injected in one labeled
case. It confirms that decoded read eligibility is retained and the subsequent
real write/read stream remains exact. All other TLS cases use real library
results, not simulated WANT classifications.

The new net.h comments document stable retry bytes and precedence. This is an
API-contract/robustness correction; do not report a demonstrated crash or a
new authentication bypass.

Evidence: the write-priority, write-priority12, want-read and reset-write
records in the same TLS result files.

3. CONFIRMED CHILD-OWNERSHIP DEFECT: INHERITED AUTOMATIC REAPING

Resolver cleanup uses its direct child PID for cancellation and waits to pin
that identity. An inherited SIGCHLD=SIG_IGN or SA_NOCLDWAIT discards a child
identity automatically on exit, before the client necessarily collects the
result. The baseline accepted those policies, forked a helper, allowed it to
auto-exit, and then attempted SIGKILL against its stale numeric PID during
net_close. The fixture observes this actual call after proving its own child
no longer exists. It does not force PID reuse or signal an unrelated process.

The candidate checks sigaction at the resolver creation boundary before making
any pipe or child. Auto-reaping is rejected with an actionable launcher error.
Ordinary default handling and a non-reaping custom handler are accepted; the
existing cancellation path collects those children normally. The caller must
continue to leave child ownership intact and not reap these children itself.
The client does not change SIGCHLD policy later. The fixture restores every
incoming signal disposition after its case.

All three unsafe dispositions were accepted by the baseline, each with one
pipe, one fork, and one stale-PID signal attempt. Candidate rejects each with
zero pipes/forks/signals. Two safe dispositions start and cancel normally.
Normal and sanitizer results match. On Linux a live ignored child did not make
WNOHANG return ECHILD immediately; the reproduced problem is after automatic
exit/reaping, correcting that earlier inspection hypothesis.

Evidence: final-baseline-ownership.json, final-*-ownership-normal.json and
final-*-resolver_ownership-sanitize.json.

4. RETAINED SECURITY CONTROLS AND REVIEW

The existing transport suite still passes plaintext byte integrity, TLS DNS/IP
identity, wrong identity, untrusted CA, expired certificate, setup deadlines,
resolver descriptor isolation including high FDs above lowered limits, and
cancellation/deadline reaping. All 31 reconnect-classification cases still pass,
including DNS categories, socket errors, handshake EOF, clean/unnotified TLS
EOF, protocol failures, bad descriptors and earlier-address refusal followed
by TLS policy failure. Normal and genuinely instrumented ASan/UBSan outputs are captured separately
for both clients. The exact compiler arguments and ASan/UBSan symbols in all
12 sanitizer compilation outputs (including retry objects) were inspected.

No new certificate bypass, CA downgrade, resolver descriptor leak, or unsafe
plaintext fallback was confirmed. Source review checked pinned write buffers,
handshake directions, resolver cancellation/reaping and descriptor replacement.
This is bounded review and testing, not a claim that those paths are defect-free.
Root and the local-security agent independently reviewed the net.c changes and
application integration; no further concrete blocker was reported.

5. EXECUTION, LIMITS AND EXACT REPRODUCTION

Executed on Linux with GCC 14.2 and OpenSSL 3.5.7. No native OpenBSD or LibreSSL
runtime result is claimed. The TLS fixture has a compile-only capability check
for the adversarial server APIs (KeyUpdate/memory BIO). Unsupported development
libraries report UNAVAILABLE, exit 77, before claiming TLS execution.
Production changes use the longstanding clear-mode/read-ahead interfaces.
The ownership fixture uses POSIX signals, forks and pipes and makes no DNS call.

ASan/UBSan used:
  CFLAGS='-O1 -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer'
  LDFLAGS='-fsanitize=address,undefined'
  ASAN_OPTIONS='detect_leaks=0:halt_on_error=1'
  UBSAN_OPTIONS='halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=1'
Leak scanning remains unavailable in this environment and is not claimed.
TLS library internals are the installed system library, not rebuilt under ASan.

New ordinary gates, from either candidate root:
  python3 tests/test_net_tls_budget.py
  python3 tests/test_net_resolver_ownership.py
The first defaults to 10,000 valid control records; --updates 100000 reproduces
the larger diagnostic. Both accept --report PATH and --source-root PATH for
explicit baseline comparison without modifying the source under test.

The exact final commands, environments, outputs, elapsed times and hashes are
in final-command-results.json and its named per-gate JSON/log files. The wrapper
run_final.py captures the initial sequence; rerun_retained_instrumentation.py
records the corrected retained-harness runs and trace_cc.py only observes
compiler arguments/output symbols, without injecting flags. net.c.diff and
net.h.diff contain only this agent's production changes. Initial exploratory
probes are separate from final validation. One exploratory write probe wrongly
assumed every partial write was exactly 16 KiB; it was corrected to accept the
actual positive progress and check complete-stream integrity. That fixture
assumption was not a product defect and is not counted as a security finding.

Validation correction discovered during independent cross-review:
The old test_net.py and test_net_retry.py ignored CFLAGS/LDFLAGS and hardcoded
-O2. The first two records named retained-*-sanitize therefore were redundant
normal runs, not sanitizer executions. Their original commands and outputs are
preserved in final-command-results.json with explicit not-instrumented labels;
they are excluded from the final sanitizer count. No defect is hidden by that
reclassification. Both harnesses now parse CC/CPPFLAGS/CFLAGS/LDFLAGS for every
compiled fixture while retaining normal defaults. Both clients then passed
both retained suites again normally and with actual ASan/UBSan instrumentation.
The observing compiler wrapper added no flags; it recorded the harness-supplied
flags and independently verified __asan_init and __ubsan_handle_* references
in every instrumented output. All four genuine retained sanitizer gates pass.
The four new targeted sanitizer gates already honored flags and remain valid.

Official references checked during review:
  https://docs.openssl.org/3.5/man3/SSL_CTX_set_mode/
  https://docs.openssl.org/3.5/man3/SSL_CTX_set_read_ahead/
  https://docs.openssl.org/3.5/man3/SSL_pending/
  https://docs.openssl.org/3.5/man3/SSL_get_error/
  https://docs.openssl.org/3.5/man3/SSL_write/
  https://man.openbsd.org/OpenBSD-6.8/SSL_set_mode.3
  https://github.com/libressl/openbsd/blob/master/src/lib/libtls/tls.c

6. READ-ONLY PRESENCE CROSS-REVIEW

After transport validation, root assigned a separate read-only review of the
state owner's presence changes. Two concrete candidate-ordering defects were
reproduced: local activity recorded before /cancel was lost when restoring a
masked automatic-away state; and delayed 305 for an earlier BACK retired the
pending intent of an already-sent later AWAY, allowing automatic detach text
to override it. The state owner fixed both and expanded its regressions.
Both independent private probes now pass against app.c SHA256
4464bb46c0584cc36ba77f6f580113d84a6ab9b73fcc919457e3fc01de373651.
No further concrete issue was found in the reviewed timer, cancellation,
first-write and ownership paths. No app.c edit was made by this reviewer.
Evidence and limits: presence-cross-review.txt and presence-cross-review-fixed.json.
Earlier failed candidate probes remain preserved separately. These are
controlled application-state tests, not live-network/terminal evidence.

PRESENCE STATE CROSS-REVIEW
Date: 2026-11-16 UTC
Reviewer: transport agent, read-only application review

Reviewed final app.c SHA256:
4464bb46c0584cc36ba77f6f580113d84a6ab9b73fcc919457e3fc01de373651
The onekeyirc/vipirc app.c and app.h copies match. No application production
changes were made by this reviewer.

Two concrete ordering defects were reproduced against the initial state-owner
candidate (app.c SHA256 4543e24547bae3e4264f04a388a6f49dce01020f73b580c91418cd1cfb37ecdc),
then fixed by that owner and independently retested here:

1. Local activity before cancellation
A script AWAY queued behind a blocked control frame temporarily masked a
previously confirmed automatic idle-away state. Real frontends report local
activity before dispatching /cancel. The old candidate restored the prior
idle-away snapshot on cancellation but lost that already-observed activity;
no clearing AWAY was sent. A private copy of the existing restore-idle case
moved activity before cancellation and failed its exact wire-output check.

The final implementation records a latent clear request/deadline in the exact
owned rollback frame when local activity occurs. It preserves the queued
script's present priority, yet cancellation/rejection restores the current
clear intent. Prior manual away is not converted into automatic clear. The
private frontend-order probe now passes and emits the single expected AWAY
clear after the held PING. The state owner's broader tests cover foregrounding,
renewed background state, rejection and server-confirmation variants.

2. Earlier 305 while a later AWAY awaits 306
The probe sends BACK, then a script AWAY, then receives the delayed 305 for
BACK. The old candidate cleared manual_away_pending for the later AWAY. A
detach then appended an automatic Detached AWAY over the explicit script text.
This case occurs after the script frame has completed writing, so the queued
rollback pointer cannot represent that outstanding server confirmation.

The final code lets 305 update observed away=false while retaining outstanding
nonempty manual AWAY intent; 306 acknowledges that intent. A newer explicit
BACK already clears it. The same distinction is applied to the rollback
snapshot. The private probe now reports manual_away_pending=1 after the older
305 and sends only the requested script AWAY across detach.

Final independent private probe result: both compile and run successfully.
Exact commands, outputs, binary hashes and unchanged-source check are recorded
in presence-cross-review-fixed.json. Failing candidate observations are kept in
presence-activity-cross-review.json and presence-sent-confirmation-cross-review.json.
These are deterministic real-application fixtures with a controlled in-memory
transport/fake clock, not a live IRC or terminal integration claim. No duplicate
stress run or broad new application test was performed by this reviewer.

Additional read-only findings: no further concrete blocker found. Failure to
queue a clear schedules a bounded one-second retry. Poll deadlines and finite
write/read batches remain intact. Cancellation restores only the current owned
unsent presence frame; fit rejection restores before freeing. A first write
attempt, including a zero-byte TLS retry, retires rollback ownership while
retaining the in-flight bytes required by SSL_write. Queue clear, disconnect
and free retire the owner before releasing frames. Manual/script intent stays
separate from observed server away state under the reviewed delayed numerics.
This scoped review and two regressions are not proof against all orderings.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Preserve the earlier mislabel, then record genuine retained sanitizer gates."""
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import time

out = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
workspace = out.parents[1]
summary = out / "final-command-results.json"
report = json.loads(summary.read_text())
for entry in report["commands"]:
    if entry["label"] in ("retained-test_net-sanitize", "retained-test_net_retry-sanitize"):
        entry["instrumentation_status"] = "not instrumented: legacy harness ignored CFLAGS/LDFLAGS"
        entry["validation_classification"] = "development redundant normal run; excluded from sanitizer claims"
report["validation_correction"] = "The two historical retained *-sanitize entries were normal runs because the old harness ignored flags. They are preserved and superseded by the explicit verified-instrumentation entries."
flags = {"CFLAGS": "-g -O1 -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer",
         "LDFLAGS": "-fsanitize=address,undefined", "ASAN_OPTIONS": "detect_leaks=0:halt_on_error=1",
         "UBSAN_OPTIONS": "halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=1"}
for project in ("onekeyirc-0.1.27", "vipirc-0.7.28"):
    root = workspace / "irc-deep-work" / project
    for script in ("test_net.py", "test_net_retry.py"):
        for sanitize in (False, True):
            label = "retained-corrected-" + project + "-" + Path(script).stem + ("-sanitize" if sanitize else "-normal")
            trace = out / (label + "-compile.json")
            environment = dict(flags) if sanitize else {}
            environment.update({"CC": sys.executable + " " + str(out / "trace_cc.py"),
                                "IRC_REVIEW_BUILD_TRACE": str(trace),
                                "IRC_REVIEW_REQUIRE_SANITIZERS": "1" if sanitize else "0"})
            effective = os.environ.copy(); effective.update(environment)
            command = [sys.executable, str(root / "tests" / script)]
            started = time.monotonic()
            process = subprocess.run(command, cwd=root, env=effective, text=True, capture_output=True, timeout=90)
            builds = json.loads(trace.read_text()) if trace.exists() else []
            entry = {"label": label, "command": command, "cwd": str(root), "environment_delta": environment,
                     "returncode": process.returncode, "expected_returncode": 0,
                     "matched_expected_outcome": process.returncode == 0,
                     "elapsed_seconds": time.monotonic() - started,
                     "stdout": process.stdout, "stderr": process.stderr, "compiler_trace": builds,
                     "instrumentation_status": "ASan and UBSan symbols verified in every output" if sanitize else "normal",
                     "input_sha256": {str(root / name): hashlib.sha256((root / name).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
                                      for name in ("src/net.c", "src/net.h", "tests/" + script)}}
            report["commands"].append(entry)
            (out / (label + ".log")).write_text(process.stdout + process.stderr, encoding="utf-8")
            summary.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="ascii")
            print(label, process.returncode, "compile outputs", len(builds), flush=True)
            if process.returncode:
                print(process.stdout + process.stderr, flush=True)
for project in ("onekeyirc-0.1.27", "vipirc-0.7.28"):
    for script in ("test_net.py", "test_net_retry.py"):
        path = workspace / "irc-deep-work" / project / "tests" / script
        report["candidate_source_sha256"][str(path)] = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
report["matched_all_expected_outcomes"] = all(entry["matched_expected_outcome"] for entry in report["commands"])
summary.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="ascii")
print("all_expected_outcomes", report["matched_all_expected_outcomes"], flush=True)

network/run_final.py.contents:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Capture exact transport-only final commands and baseline/fixed outcomes."""
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import time

workspace = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
out = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
one = workspace / "irc-deep-work/onekeyirc-0.1.27"
vip = workspace / "irc-deep-work/vipirc-0.7.28"
base = workspace / "irc-deep-baseline/onekeyirc-0.1.26"
files = ["src/net.c", "src/net.h", "tests/test_net_tls_budget.c", "tests/test_net_tls_budget.py",
         "tests/test_net_resolver_ownership.c", "tests/test_net_resolver_ownership.py"]
digest = lambda p: hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
hashes = {str(root / name): digest(root / name) for root in (one, vip) for name in files}
baseline_hashes = {str(base / name): digest(base / name) for name in ("src/net.c", "src/net.h")}
result = {"commands": [], "candidate_source_sha256": hashes, "baseline_source_sha256": baseline_hashes,
          "source_copies_identical": all((one / name).read_bytes() == (vip / name).read_bytes() for name in files)}
sanitizer = {"CFLAGS": "-O1 -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer",
             "LDFLAGS": "-fsanitize=address,undefined", "ASAN_OPTIONS": "detect_leaks=0:halt_on_error=1",
             "UBSAN_OPTIONS": "halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=1"}

def run(label, command, *, environment=None, expected=0, cwd=workspace):
    effective = os.environ.copy()
    effective.update(environment or {})
    started = time.monotonic()
    process = subprocess.run(command, cwd=cwd, env=effective, text=True, capture_output=True, timeout=180)
    entry = {"label": label, "command": command, "cwd": str(cwd), "environment_delta": environment or {},
             "expected_returncode": expected, "returncode": process.returncode,
             "elapsed_seconds": time.monotonic() - started, "stdout": process.stdout, "stderr": process.stderr,
             "matched_expected_outcome": process.returncode == expected}
    result["commands"].append(entry)
    (out / (label + ".log")).write_text(process.stdout + process.stderr, encoding="utf-8")
    (out / "final-command-results.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="ascii")
    print(label, "EXPECTED" if process.returncode == expected else "UNEXPECTED", process.returncode, flush=True)
    for line in process.stdout.splitlines():
        if '"case":"budget"' in line or '"stale_pid_signal_calls"' in line:
            print(line, flush=True)


for command in (["cc", "--version"], ["openssl", "version", "-a"]):
    run("environment-" + command[0], command)
run("final-baseline-tls", [sys.executable, str(one / "tests/test_net_tls_budget.py"), "--source-root", str(base),
                          "--updates", "100000", "--report", str(out / "final-baseline-tls.json")], expected=1)
run("final-one-tls-normal", [sys.executable, str(one / "tests/test_net_tls_budget.py"), "--updates", "100000",
                            "--report", str(out / "final-one-tls-normal.json")])
run("final-baseline-ownership", [sys.executable, str(one / "tests/test_net_resolver_ownership.py"), "--source-root", str(base),
                                "--report", str(out / "final-baseline-ownership.json")], expected=1)
for label, root in (("one", one), ("vip", vip)):
    if label != "one":
        run("final-" + label + "-tls-normal", [sys.executable, str(root / "tests/test_net_tls_budget.py"),
                                              "--report", str(out / ("final-" + label + "-tls-normal.json"))])
    run("final-" + label + "-ownership-normal", [sys.executable, str(root / "tests/test_net_resolver_ownership.py"),
                                                "--report", str(out / ("final-" + label + "-ownership-normal.json"))])
    for test in ("tls_budget", "resolver_ownership"):
        gate = "final-" + label + "-" + test + "-sanitize"
        run(gate, [sys.executable, str(root / ("tests/test_net_" + test + ".py")), "--report", str(out / (gate + ".json"))], environment=sanitizer)
for test in ("test_net.py", "test_net_retry.py"):
    run("retained-" + Path(test).stem + "-normal", [sys.executable, str(one / "tests" / test)], cwd=one)
    run("retained-" + Path(test).stem + "-sanitize", [sys.executable, str(one / "tests" / test)], environment=sanitizer, cwd=one)
result["source_unchanged_during_validation"] = all(digest(Path(name)) == value for name, value in hashes.items())
result["baseline_unchanged_during_validation"] = all(digest(Path(name)) == value for name, value in baseline_hashes.items())
result["matched_all_expected_outcomes"] = all(command["matched_expected_outcome"] for command in result["commands"])
(out / "final-command-results.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="ascii")
print(json.dumps({key: result[key] for key in ("source_copies_identical", "source_unchanged_during_validation", "baseline_unchanged_during_validation", "matched_all_expected_outcomes")}), flush=True)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Observe the exact compiler arguments without injecting build flags."""
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shlex
import subprocess
import sys

command = shlex.split(os.environ.get("IRC_REVIEW_REAL_CC", "cc")) + sys.argv[1:]
result = subprocess.run(command)
entry = {"command": command, "returncode": result.returncode,
         "source_sha256": {arg: hashlib.sha256(Path(arg).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
                           for arg in sys.argv[1:] if arg.endswith(".c") and Path(arg).is_file()}}
if result.returncode == 0 and "-o" in sys.argv:
    output = Path(sys.argv[sys.argv.index("-o") + 1])
    entry["output"] = str(output)
    entry["output_sha256"] = hashlib.sha256(output.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    symbols = subprocess.run(["nm", "-u", str(output)], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    entry["asan_init_symbol"] = "__asan_init" in symbols
    entry["ubsan_handler_symbols"] = "__ubsan_handle_" in symbols
trace = Path(os.environ["IRC_REVIEW_BUILD_TRACE"])
previous = json.loads(trace.read_text()) if trace.exists() else []
previous.append(entry)
trace.write_text(json.dumps(previous, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="ascii")
if os.environ.get("IRC_REVIEW_REQUIRE_SANITIZERS") == "1" and result.returncode == 0:
    if not entry.get("asan_init_symbol") or not entry.get("ubsan_handler_symbols"):
        raise SystemExit("Expected ASan/UBSan instrumentation symbols are absent.")
raise SystemExit(result.returncode)
