#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Create source-only packages from the verified upstream file inventories."""
from datetime import datetime, timezone
import gzip
import hashlib
import io
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import stat
import subprocess
import sys
import tarfile
import time

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
OUT = ROOT / "irc-deep-validation"
WORK = ROOT / "irc-deep-work"
BASE = ROOT / "irc-deep-baseline"
STAGE = ROOT / "irc-deep-release-staging"
RELEASE = ROOT / "irc-deep-release"
PAIRS = (("onekeyirc-0.1.26", "onekeyirc-0.1.27"),
         ("vipirc-0.7.27", "vipirc-0.7.28"))
EXTRA = ("tests/test_presence_cancellation.c", "tests/test_presence_recovery.c",
         "tests/test_credential_descendants.c", "tests/test_credential_signals.c",
         "tests/test_background_rights.c", "tests/test_net_tls_budget.c",
         "tests/test_net_tls_budget.py", "tests/test_net_resolver_ownership.c",
         "tests/test_net_resolver_ownership.py", "doc/SECURITY-DEEP-REVIEW-2026-11-16.txt",
         "doc/DEEP-TEST-RESULTS.json")
VIP_EXTRA = ()

EPOCH = int(datetime(2026, 11, 16, tzinfo=timezone.utc).timestamp())


def digest(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def paths(old):
    entries = json.loads((BASE/old/"SOURCE-MANIFEST.json").read_text())["files"]
    extra = EXTRA + (VIP_EXTRA if old.startswith("vipirc") else ())
    result = sorted(set(e["path"] for e in entries) | set(extra))
    assert len(result) == len(entries) + len(extra)
    return result


def source_hashes(tree):
    return {p.name: digest(p) for p in sorted((tree/"src").iterdir())
            if p.suffix in (".c", ".h")}


def stage():
    STAGE.mkdir(exist_ok=False)
    for old, new in PAIRS:
        for rel in paths(old):
            src, dst = WORK/new/rel, STAGE/new/rel
            assert src.is_file() and not src.is_symlink(), src
            dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            shutil.copy2(src, dst)
        print("STAGED " + new + " " + str(len(paths(old))) + " source files", flush=True)


def validate():
    tree = STAGE/"onekeyirc-0.1.27"
    install = OUT/"private-install-root"
    install.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    assert not any(p.is_file() or p.is_symlink() for p in install.rglob("*"))
    env = dict(os.environ, CPPFLAGS="-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2",
               CFLAGS="-O2 -Werror -fstack-protector-strong -Wformat=2 -Werror=format-security -fPIE",
               LDFLAGS="-pie -Wl,-z,relro -Wl,-z,now -Wl,-z,noexecstack")
    records = []
    for name, cmd in (
        ("configure", ["./configure"]),
        ("strict-build", ["make", "onekeyirc"]),
        ("install", ["make", "install", "DESTDIR="+str(install)])):
        start = time.monotonic()
        log = OUT/("package-"+name+".log")
        with log.open("wb") as stream:
            p = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=tree, env=env, stdout=stream,
                               stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, timeout=180)
        records.append(dict(name=name, command=cmd, exit_code=p.returncode,
                            seconds=round(time.monotonic()-start,3), log=log.name))
        assert p.returncode == 0, log.read_text()
    installed = []
    for p in sorted(install.rglob("*")):
        if p.is_file():
            rel = p.relative_to(install)
            expected = 0o755 if str(rel).endswith("/bin/onekeyirc") else 0o644
            assert stat.S_IMODE(p.stat().st_mode) == expected, p
            installed.append(dict(path=str(rel), mode=oct(expected), sha256=digest(p)))
    for name in ("SECURITY-DEEP-REVIEW-2026-11-16.txt", "DEEP-TEST-RESULTS.json"):
        assert (install/"usr/local/share/doc/onekeyirc"/name).read_bytes() == (tree/"doc"/name).read_bytes()
    assert (install/"usr/local/bin/onekeyirc").read_bytes() == (tree/"onekeyirc").read_bytes()
    version_output = subprocess.check_output([str(tree/"onekeyirc"), "--version"], env=env).decode()
    version = version_output.splitlines()[0]
    assert version == "onekeyirc 0.1.27", version
    manual = subprocess.check_output([str(tree/"onekeyirc"), "--manual"], env=env)
    assert manual == (tree/"doc/onekeyirc-manual.txt").read_bytes()
    with (OUT/"package-uninstall.log").open("wb") as stream:
        p = subprocess.run(["make", "uninstall", "DESTDIR="+str(install)],
                           cwd=tree, env=env, stdout=stream, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, timeout=30)
    assert p.returncode == 0
    assert not any(p.is_file() or p.is_symlink() for p in install.rglob("*"))
    result = dict(status="PASS", scope="clean standalone source build and private DESTDIR install/uninstall; no host installation",
                  records=records, installed_files=installed, version=version, version_output=version_output,
                  manual_matches=True, uninstall_left_files=False,
                  tested_binary_sha256=digest(WORK/"onekeyirc-0.1.27/onekeyirc"),
                  staged_binary_sha256=digest(tree/"onekeyirc"),
                  identical_tested_binary=digest(tree/"onekeyirc")==digest(WORK/"onekeyirc-0.1.27/onekeyirc"),
                  source_hashes={new:source_hashes(STAGE/new) for _,new in PAIRS},
                  validated_file_sha256={new:{rel:digest(STAGE/new/rel) for rel in paths(old)
                      if rel not in ("doc/SECURITY-DEEP-REVIEW-2026-11-16.txt","doc/DEEP-TEST-RESULTS.json","doc/VALIDATION.txt")}
                      for old,new in PAIRS},
                  note="Initial staged installation precedes insertion of packaging evidence into audit documents. Final finalized-document installation is checked again during archive creation.")
    (OUT/"packaging-validation.json").write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2)+"\n")
    print("PASS: clean build, version/manual, private installation modes/content, and uninstall", flush=True)
    print("Bit-identical to tested onekeyirc binary: " + str(result["identical_tested_binary"]), flush=True)


def finish():
    validation = json.loads((OUT/"packaging-validation.json").read_text())
    assert validation["status"] == "PASS"
    RELEASE.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    archive_results = []
    for old, new in PAIRS:
        tree = STAGE/new
        assert source_hashes(WORK/new) == validation["source_hashes"][new], "source changed after staged validation"
        for rel, expected in validation["validated_file_sha256"][new].items():
            assert digest(WORK/new/rel) == expected, "validated file changed: "+rel
        for rel in paths(old):
            shutil.copy2(WORK/new/rel, tree/rel)
        if new == "onekeyirc-0.1.27":
            install = OUT/"private-install-root"
            assert not any(p.is_file() or p.is_symlink() for p in install.rglob("*"))
            with (OUT/"package-final-doc-install.log").open("wb") as stream:
                subprocess.run(["make","install","DESTDIR="+str(install)], cwd=tree,
                               stdout=stream,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,check=True,timeout=30)
            installed = {str(p.relative_to(install)):p for p in install.rglob("*") if p.is_file()}
            assert set(installed) == {r["path"] for r in validation["installed_files"]}
            for rel, actual in installed.items():
                if rel.endswith("/bin/onekeyirc"):
                    source=tree/"onekeyirc"; mode=0o755
                elif "/man/man1/" in rel:
                    source=tree/"doc/onekeyirc.1"; mode=0o644
                else:
                    name=actual.name;mode=0o644

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Maintain current release metadata while retaining historical evidence."""
import json
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
PAIRS = (("onekeyirc", "0.1.26", "0.1.27"), ("vipirc", "0.7.27", "0.7.28"))
REPORT = "SECURITY-DEEP-REVIEW-2026-11-16.txt"
RESULTS = "DEEP-TEST-RESULTS.json"
intro = """This release improves TLS event-loop fairness, credential-helper cleanup and
child-process ownership, and repairs presence recovery under send-queue pressure.
It includes reproducible regressions and separate security, efficiency and
stability evidence in [the current review](doc/SECURITY-DEEP-REVIEW-2026-11-16.txt).

It retains one local reminder per running client:
"""
entry = """- Yield between TLS control records so one read cannot bypass the event-loop
  budget; keep read-ahead disabled and preserve decoded-data wakeups.
- Respect pending TLS write retries before other TLS I/O, including poll and
  pending-data behavior while a write waits for socket space.
- Retain credential-helper process ownership until both result pipes finish;
  cancel and timeout can then stop a same-group descendant that holds a pipe.
- Refuse helper/resolver startup under an auto-reaping SIGCHLD policy, before
  creating child resources, rather than retaining an unsafe numeric identity.
- Restore current presence intent when an unsent scripted AWAY/BACK is
  cancelled or rejected; account for delayed confirmations of earlier commands.
- Retry a failed automatic-away clear after reattach/local activity at a bounded
  interval, while preserving newer manual/script/background intent.
- Add real loopback TLS and native socketpair/SCM_RIGHTS regressions, controlled
  helper tests, and normal/sanitizer make check-deep targets. The full ncurses,
  native named-socket session lifecycle and native OpenBSD limits are explicit.
"""
security = """## Current continuation

The transport yields between TLS control records and follows write-retry
ordering. The bounded-loopback evidence separates availability improvements
from certificate verification; verification remains required for credential use.

Credential helpers retain their direct-child ownership while either output
pipe remains open. This allows cancellation to stop same-group inherited pipe
writers. Helpers are trusted external programs, not sandboxes: a descendant
that deliberately changes process groups is outside this cleanup guarantee.
Resolver and credential starts reject SIGCHLD=SIG_IGN or SA_NOCLDWAIT rather
than relying on a child identity that the operating system can auto-reap.
The client itself does not install a reaping SIGCHLD handler. Embedding these
modules in a process that independently reaps their children is unsupported.

Automatic-away retries are timed and yield to newer accepted presence intent.
Cancelling a queued script command cannot cancel a partially written IRC line.
The review includes source-level ownership checks and executed regressions;
it does not certify that either client is free of vulnerabilities.

"""
for app, old, new in PAIRS:
    base = ROOT/"irc-deep-work"/(app + "-" + new)
    for rel in ("README.md", "INSTALL", "SECURITY.md", "doc/" + app + ".1"):
        path = base/rel
        text = path.read_text()
        assert old in text, (path, old)
        path.write_text(text.replace(old, new))
    path = base/"README.md"
    text = path.read_text()
    before = "This follow-up release strengthens automatic-away scheduling and private\ncommand-history filtering, and detects replaced or rewritten catch-up anchors.\nIt also adds one local reminder per running client:\n"
    assert text.count(before) == 1
    text = text.replace(before, intro)
    text = text.replace("See [the follow-up review and validation]", "The preceding [follow-up review and validation]")
    text = text.replace("(doc/SECURITY-FOLLOWUP-2026-11-16.txt).\nThe preceding security", "(doc/SECURITY-FOLLOWUP-2026-11-16.txt) is retained.\nThe earlier security")
    path.write_text(text)
    path = base/"SECURITY.md"
    text = path.read_text()
    before = "Current review: [2026-11-16 security follow-up](doc/SECURITY-FOLLOWUP-2026-11-16.txt).\nExact follow-up results and limits are recorded in doc/FOLLOWUP-TEST-RESULTS.json.\n"
    after = ("Current review: [2026-11-16 deep continuation](doc/" + REPORT + ").\n"
             "Exact current results and limits are recorded in doc/" + RESULTS + ".\n"
             "The preceding follow-up is retained in doc/SECURITY-FOLLOWUP-2026-11-16.txt\n"
             "and doc/FOLLOWUP-TEST-RESULTS.json.\n")
    assert before in text
    text = text.replace(before, after)
    marker = "## Existing security controls\n"
    assert marker in text
    path.write_text(text.replace(marker, security + marker, 1))
    path = base/"CHANGELOG.md"
    text = path.read_text()
    first, rest = text.split("\n\n", 1)
    path.write_text(first + "\n\n## " + new + " - 2026-11-16 (UTC)\n\n" + entry + "\n" + rest)
    path = base/"Makefile.in"
    text = path.read_text()
    old_files = "doc/SECURITY-FOLLOWUP-2026-11-16.txt doc/FOLLOWUP-TEST-RESULTS.json"
    new_files = old_files + " doc/" + REPORT + " doc/" + RESULTS
    assert text.count(old_files) == 1
    text = text.replace(old_files, new_files)
    old_names = '"$(DESTDIR)$(DOCDIR)/SECURITY-FOLLOWUP-2026-11-16.txt" "$(DESTDIR)$(DOCDIR)/FOLLOWUP-TEST-RESULTS.json"'
    new_names = old_names + ' "$(DESTDIR)$(DOCDIR)/' + REPORT + '" "$(DESTDIR)$(DOCDIR)/' + RESULTS + '"'
    assert text.count(old_names) == 2
    path.write_text(text.replace(old_names, new_names))
    # These are filled with validated evidence before staging/install checks.
    (base/"doc"/REPORT).write_text("Review assembly pending final release gates.\n")
    (base/"doc"/RESULTS).write_text("{}\n")

vip = ROOT/"irc-deep-work/vipirc-0.7.28"
path = vip/"doc/manual.txt"
text = path.read_text().replace("0.7.27", "0.7.28").replace("0.1.26", "0.1.27")
text += """

SECURITY AND PRESENCE CONTINUATION

The current source includes TLS control-record fairness and write-retry
ordering, bounded credential-helper cleanup, and child-ownership checks.
If a launcher ignores SIGCHLD or enables automatic child reaping, helper or
resolver startup fails with an ownership error. Use normal waitable-child
handling in the launcher; the client does not change that global policy.

When an unsent scripted AWAY or BACK is cancelled, the preceding still-current
presence intent is restored. A delayed confirmation for an earlier command
does not acknowledge a script frame which has not been sent. A failed clear of
automatic away after reattach or local activity is retried at a bounded rate.
Newer manual presence choices continue to take priority.

The exact executed tests and remaining platform limits are in
doc/SECURITY-DEEP-REVIEW-2026-11-16.txt and doc/DEEP-TEST-RESULTS.json.
Use make check-deep for the new bounded regressions. The real TLS fixture
reports UNAVAILABLE when its development-library APIs are unsupported.
"""
path.write_text(text)
manual = '#include <stddef.h>\n#include "manual.h"\n\nconst char *const vipirc_manual[] = {\n'
manual += "".join("    " + json.dumps(line, ensure_ascii=True) + ",\n" for line in text.splitlines())
manual += "    NULL\n};\n"
(vip/"src/manual.c").write_text(manual)
print("Updated current documentation; retained all historical reports.")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run and record the final scoped release checks for this continuation."""
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import platform
import subprocess
import sys
import time

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
OUT = ROOT / "irc-deep-validation"
ONE = ROOT / "irc-deep-work/onekeyirc-0.1.27"
VIP = ROOT / "irc-deep-work/vipirc-0.7.28"
RESULT = OUT / "deep-gates.json"
ENV = dict(os.environ, ASAN_OPTIONS="detect_leaks=0:halt_on_error=1",
           UBSAN_OPTIONS="halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=1",
           ONEKEY_BINARY=str(ONE / "onekeyirc"), VIPIRC_IDLE_BINARY="")
BASE = ["cc", "-D_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L", "-D_XOPEN_SOURCE=700",
        "-D_XOPEN_SOURCE_EXTENDED=1", "-std=c11", "-Wall", "-Wextra",
        "-Wpedantic", "-Werror", "-Wformat=2", "-Werror=format-security", "-Isrc"]
HARD = ["-O2", "-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2", "-fstack-protector-strong", "-fPIE",
        "-pie", "-Wl,-z,relro", "-Wl,-z,now", "-Wl,-z,noexecstack"]
SAN = ["-O1", "-g", "-fsanitize=address,undefined", "-fno-omit-frame-pointer"]
BUILD_ENV = dict(ENV, CPPFLAGS="-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2",
                 CFLAGS="-O2 -Werror -fstack-protector-strong -Wformat=2 -Werror=format-security -fPIE",
                 LDFLAGS="-pie -Wl,-z,relro -Wl,-z,now -Wl,-z,noexecstack")
records = json.loads(RESULT.read_text()) if RESULT.exists() else []


def sha(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def inputs():
    result = {}
    for tree in (ONE, VIP):
        digest = hashlib.sha256()
        paths = [tree/"configure", tree/"Makefile.in"]
        paths += [p for area in ("src", "tests") for p in (tree/area).iterdir()
                  if p.is_file() and p.suffix in (".c", ".h", ".py")]
        for path in sorted(paths):
            digest.update(str(path.relative_to(tree)).encode() + b"\0")
            digest.update(path.read_bytes())
            digest.update(b"\0")
        result[tree.name] = digest.hexdigest()
    return result


def run(name, command, cwd=ONE, env=None, timeout=300, accepted=(0,)):
    prior = next((r for r in reversed(records) if r["name"] == name), None)
    if os.environ.get("AUDIT_SKIP_PASS") == "1" and prior and prior["status"] == "PASS":
        print("RETAIN " + name, flush=True)
        return
    log = OUT / (name + ".log")
    if log.exists():
        old = OUT / (name + ".previous-" + str(sum(r["name"] == name for r in records)) + ".log")
        old.write_bytes(log.read_bytes())
        if prior:
            prior["log"] = old.name
    print("RUN " + name, flush=True)
    before = inputs()
    start = time.monotonic()
    expired = False
    with log.open("wb") as stream:
        try:
            result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=cwd, env=env or ENV,
                                    stdout=stream, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, timeout=timeout)
            code = result.returncode
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            code = 124
            expired = True
    record = dict(name=name, command=command, cwd=str(cwd),
                  seconds=round(time.monotonic()-start, 3), exit_code=code,
                  log=log.name, timeout=expired,
                  inputs_before=before, inputs_after=inputs(),
                  status="UNAVAILABLE" if code == 77 else "PASS" if code == 0 else "FAIL")
    if record["inputs_before"] != record["inputs_after"]:
        record["status"] = "SUPERSEDED"
    records.append(record)
    RESULT.write_text(json.dumps(records, indent=2) + "\n")
    print(record["status"] + " " + name + " " + str(record["seconds"]) + "s", flush=True)
    if code not in accepted or record["status"] == "SUPERSEDED":
        print(log.read_text(errors="replace")[-7000:], flush=True)
        raise SystemExit(code or 1)


def build():
    run("release-configure", ["./configure"], env=BUILD_ENV)
    run("release-strict-build", ["make", "onekeyirc"], env=BUILD_ENV)
    stub = OUT / "unused_curses_entrypoints.c"
    stub.write_text('''#include <stdlib.h>
#include "ui.h"
int ui_welcome(int force) { (void)force; abort(); }
int ui_run_session(Client *c, Background *b, DccManager *d, int start,
                   int connect, int no_connect, int *next) {
    (void)c; (void)b; (void)d; (void)start; (void)connect;
    (void)no_connect; (void)next; abort();
}
''')
    src = next(line.split("=", 1)[1].split() for line in
               (ONE/"Makefile.in").read_text().splitlines() if line.startswith("SRC = "))
    run("release-one-sanitize-build", BASE + SAN + ["-DONEKEY_ONLY", "-o",
        str(OUT/"onekeyirc-sanitize")] + src + ["-lssl", "-lcrypto"])
    for label, flags in (("normal", HARD), ("sanitize", SAN)):
        run("release-vip-idle-" + label + "-build", BASE + flags + ["-o",
            str(OUT/("vipirc-idle-" + label))] + src + ["src/manual.c", str(stub),
            "-lssl", "-lcrypto"], cwd=VIP)
    for binary, args, target in (
        (ONE/"onekeyirc", ["--manual"], ONE/"doc/onekeyirc-manual.txt"),
        (OUT/"vipirc-idle-normal", ["-i", "--manual"], VIP/"doc/vipirc-idle-manual.txt")):
        target.write_bytes(subprocess.check_output([str(binary), *args], env=ENV))
    full = subprocess.check_output([str(OUT/"vipirc-idle-normal"), "--manual"], env=ENV)
    assert full == (VIP/"doc/manual.txt").read_bytes(), "full manual embedding mismatch"
    hashes = {str(p.relative_to(ROOT)): sha(p) for p in
              (ONE/"onekeyirc", OUT/"onekeyirc-sanitize", OUT/"vipirc-idle-normal", OUT/"vipirc-idle-sanitize")}
    (OUT/"final-binary-hashes.json").write_text(json.dumps(hashes, indent=2) + "\n")
    environment = dict(date_utc="2026-11-16", platform=platform.platform(),
                       python=sys.version, compiler=subprocess.check_output(["cc", "--version"]).decode(),
                       openssl=subprocess.check_output(["openssl", "version", "-a"]).decode(),
                       sanitizers="ASan and UBSan; LeakSanitizer disabled because unavailable under tracing",
                       full_curses="Headers absent; full frontend not compiled or run",
                       vip_idle="Production idle frontend/core/main; unused curses entries abort if called")
    (OUT/"environment.json").write_text(json.dumps(environment, indent=2) + "\n")


def normal():
    for name, target in (("security", "check-security"), ("efficiency", "check-efficiency"),
                         ("session-controls", "check-session-controls"), ("detach", "check-security-detach")):
        run("release-" + name + "-normal", ["make", target], timeout=600)
    run("release-compat-units-build", ["make", "build/test_app", "build/test_credentials"])
    for name in ("test_app", "test_credentials"):
        run("release-" + name, ["./build/" + name])
    for name, args in (
        ("cli", ["tests/test_idle_cli.py"]),
        ("commands", ["tests/test_idle_commands.py"]),
        ("setup-async", ["tests/test_setup_async.py", "--mode", "one"]),
        ("setup-paths", ["tests/test_setup_paths.py", "--mode", "one"]),
        ("autojoin-reconnect", ["tests/test_autojoin.py", "--mode", "onekey", "--binary", "./onekeyirc"]),
        ("wrapping", ["tests/test_idle_wrapping.py", "--binary", "./onekeyirc"]),
        ("notice", ["tests/test_session_notice.py", "--binary", "./onekeyirc"]),
        ("terminal-policy", ["tests/test_terminal_signals.py", "--binary", "./onekeyirc"])):
        run("release-" + name, ["python3"] + args, timeout=300)
    run("release-native-session-probe", ["python3", "tests/test_session_hangup.py",
        "--binary", "./onekeyirc"], accepted=(0, 77), timeout=30)


def sanitize():
    run("release-security-sanitize", ["make", "check-security-sanitize"], timeout=600)
    run("release-session-controls-sanitize", ["make", "check-session-controls-sanitize"], timeout=300)
    run("release-one-sanitize-availability", ["python3", "tests/test_idle_availability.py",
        "--binary", str(OUT/"onekeyirc-sanitize")], timeout=180)
    for label in ("normal", "sanitize"):
        binary = OUT/("vipirc-idle-" + label)
        env = dict(ENV, VIPIRC_IDLE_BINARY=str(binary), VIPIRC_SOURCE_ROOT=str(VIP))
        for name, args in (
            ("cli", ["tests/test_idle_cli.py"]),
            ("commands", ["tests/test_idle_commands.py"]),
            ("wrapping", ["tests/test_idle_wrapping.py", "--binary", str(binary), "--full"]),
            ("availability", ["tests/test_idle_availability.py", "--binary", str(binary), "--full"]),
            ("notice", ["tests/test_session_notice.py", "--binary", str(binary), "--full"]),
            ("terminal-policy", ["tests/test_terminal_signals.py", "--binary", str(binary), "--full"])):
            run("release-vip-idle-" + label + "-" + name, ["python3"] + args, env=env)


def vip_core():
    # These targets use the real shared source and do not link curses.
    common = ["make", "-B", "-f", "Makefile.in", "CC=cc",
              "CPPFLAGS=-D_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L -D_XOPEN_SOURCE=700 -D_XOPEN_SOURCE_EXTENDED=1",
              "CFLAGS=-O2 -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror",
              "LDFLAGS=", "TLS_LIBS=-lssl -lcrypto"]
    run("release-vip-deep-normal", common + ["check-deep"], cwd=VIP, timeout=300)
    run("release-vip-deep-sanitize", common + ["check-deep-sanitize"], cwd=VIP, timeout=300)


def static():
    folder = OUT/"static"
    folder.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    result_path = folder/"results.json"
    results = json.loads(result_path.read_text()) if result_path.exists() else []
    for name in os.environ.get("STATIC_SOURCES", "app,credentials,net").split(","):
        source = ONE/"src"/(name + ".c")
        log = folder/(name + ".json")
        previous = next((r for r in reversed(results) if r["source"] == str(source.relative_to(ROOT))), None)
        if previous and previous["sha256"] == sha(source):
            print("RETAIN static " + name + " (including any recorded diagnostic)", flush=True)
            continue
        if log.exists() and previous:
            historical = folder/(name + ".previous-" + previous["sha256"][:12] + ".json")
            historical.write_bytes(log.read_bytes())
            previous["log"] = historical.name
        command = BASE + ["-O0", "-DONEKEY_ONLY", "-fanalyzer", "-fdiagnostics-format=json",
                          "-c", str(source), "-o", str(folder/(name + ".o"))]
        start = time.monotonic()
        with log.open("wb") as stream:
            result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=ONE, env=ENV, stdout=stream,
                                    stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, timeout=240)
        diagnostics = json.loads(log.read_text())
        item = dict(source=str(source.relative_to(ROOT)), sha256=sha(source), command=command,
                    seconds=round(time.monotonic()-start, 3), exit_code=result.returncode,
                    log=log.name, diagnostics=diagnostics)
        results.append(item)
        result_path.write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2) + "\n")
        assert result.returncode == 0 and diagnostics == [], item
        print("PASS static " + name, flush=True)

READ-ONLY CREDENTIAL LIFECYCLE CROSS-REVIEW
Date: 2026-11-16 UTC

Reviewed the candidate credentials.c changes against the release baseline,
test_credential_descendants.c, test_credential_signals.c, the relevant existing
test fixtures, credential headers, and negative-poll cancellation callers.
No production or test files in the credential/local task were edited here.
No new concrete issue was found in the changed ownership paths.

Observed source relationships:

- Both decryption and encryption defer waitpid until output and status have
  both reached EOF. A buffered read that has not yet observed EOF keeps the
  active direct-child slot. A read/status failure or timeout does not release
  that slot; callers subsequently cancel the job.
- Cancellation signals the owned process group and its direct child before
  marking the child retired. Retired reaping is nonblocking. A completed job
  has exited set and skips signaling, so a later job reusing the child slot
  is not targeted by cancellation of the old job.
- Child admission checks SIGCHLD before helper pipes or fork. SIG_IGN and
  SA_NOCLDWAIT are rejected; default and non-reaping handlers remain accepted.
  This relies on the task's stated no-external-reaper and no-runtime-policy-
  change contract. The current client sources wait for specifically owned
  child PIDs, rather than using an unrelated wait-for-any-child reaper.
- The descendant fixture exercises inherited stdout, status, and both writers;
  timeout and failed-status cancellation; the direct leader retained after
  exit; descendant stoppage; descriptor restoration; and normal buffered EOF
  releasing the slot. Its Linux test-only subreaper collects descendants.
- The admission fixture checks both encryption and decryption, counts helper
  forks, verifies rejected starts create no destination, and checks descriptor
  restoration. It uses controlled helpers rather than a real GPG keyring.

This is independent source/test review, not an additional execution claim.
Execution results belong to local/local-checks.json and LOCAL-REVIEW.txt.

state/final-findings.txt.contents:
BOUNDED APPLICATION STATE REVIEW
Date: 2026-11-16 UTC
Baseline: onekeyirc 0.1.26 and vipirc 0.7.27
Candidates: onekeyirc 0.1.27 and vipirc 0.7.28

Scope and result

Three ordinary presence-state defects were reproduced locally and repaired in
the mirrored shared app.c/app.h files. The new release tests are
tests/test_presence_cancellation.c and tests/test_presence_recovery.c.
Both include the existing test_app.c fixture and link app.c, autocommands.c,
sim.c and protocol.c. The transport is an in-memory test double and the
clock is deterministic. No public server, real TLS connection, fuzzing or
attack simulation was used for this review.

Final evidence is the 11 approved-* entries in release-results.json, copied
from the full development results.json. Every compile and execution returned
zero, and source_changed_during_validation is empty for all 11 groups.
The final suites contain 8 cancellation and 15 recovery scenario groups.
Both suites passed normally and with ASan/UBSan for each candidate. Existing
selected queue/presence/script/close/reconnect/roster compatibility cases
passed normally and with ASan/UBSan. The prior automatic-away retry test
also passed normally on the final shared core.

The full results.json intentionally retains expected baseline assertion
failures and intermediate development failures. Entries called final-* and
release-* are earlier development snapshots; use approved-* for the completed
code. The earlier release-results.json is preserved unchanged as
release-results-superseded-before-activity-ack.json.
In particular, background supersession and delayed 305/306 ordering guards
caught incomplete intermediate implementations before the completed gates.

Finding 1: cancelled unsent script presence retained stale intent

A configured script AWAY queued behind an ordinary blocked control write
sets manual_away_pending. Cancellation previously removed the unsent frame
but retained that flag. Configured background or idle away could then remain
suppressed. Cancelling a script BACK could also discard a prior manual-away
request or the classification of an already applied client-generated away.
Pre-write rejection after a valid line-limit update had the same cleanup gap.

Both baselines reproduced the four cancellation/rejection assertions. The
original tests for newer manual commands, server confirmation, in-flight
write preservation and reconnect already passed; these remain regression
guards rather than being described as separate baseline defects.

The fix binds a small prior-state snapshot to the exact unsent script frame.
Only that owning frame can restore it on cancellation or pre-write rejection.
A successful newer manual/client-generated presence intent releases ownership.
The first write attempt releases it, including a zero-byte TLS retry, because
that frame must finish unchanged. Reset/disconnect/free clears the owner before
further callbacks or frame cleanup. There is no queue scan for this ownership.

Delayed server confirmation needs different treatment while the owner remains
unsent: it cannot acknowledge that script frame. The owned frame's prior-state
snapshot is updated in constant time. An older 306 acknowledges prior manual
pending state while preserving prior automatic classification and a requested
clear; an older 305 records the prior state as back and removes its clear timer.
The current unsent script intent remains pending. Newer manual intent still
releases ownership. Re-detaching during a queued script cannot revive an
obsolete foreground clear when that script is subsequently cancelled.

Frontends report local activity before command dispatch. The saved prior state
therefore also records activity/foregrounding that occurs while a queued script
masks an earlier automatic-away state. Cancellation or pre-write rejection then
makes that accepted clear immediately due; a failed enqueue still schedules
the bounded one-second retry. Earlier manual away remains protected. The tests
use the actual activity-before-cancel ordering and cover server 305/306 and
renewed background intent during this interval.

Finding 2: return-to-foreground clearing was lost under control-queue pressure

After client-generated background away was applied, a full ordinary control
queue could prevent the clear requested on reattach or local activity.
The old code retained its automatic-away marker but never retried that clear
without another local action. The baseline probe drained the queue and ran
five one-second network ticks without sending the clearing AWAY.

The fix retains the current clear request and schedules its retry with the
existing one-second presence deadline. Repeated event-loop calls at the same
time do not retry. Failure schedules another bounded deadline; successful
queueing clears both request and timer. Newer accepted manual/script AWAY or
BACK, renewed background intent, server 305 and disconnect/reconnect supersede
or clear the request. An older 306 does not erase it. Disabling future automatic
away policy preserves the request to clear the automatic-away state already
applied. Script cancellation/rejection can restore a still-current prior clear
request and its deadline.

Finding 3: an older BACK acknowledgment could override newer AWAY intent

An older server 305 response to BACK previously cleared manual_away_pending
for a newer nonempty AWAY, even after that newer command had been sent.
Detaching before its 306 response could then queue background-away text over
the explicit away message. The same private probe reproduced this behavior
against the untouched baseline. A separate independent network review supplied
the initial ordering reproduction.

The current state and the owned script snapshot now distinguish the two
acknowledgments: 305 may update observed away=false, but cannot acknowledge
an outstanding nonempty AWAY. Its 306 response clears the pending flag.
An accepted newer BACK already supersedes that flag. Tests cover later manual
and script AWAY at completed-write, zero-byte retry, and partial-write stages,
plus eventual 306 and a later explicit BACK. All interaction tests retain the
original write buffer and preserve the current accepted manual intent.

Other bounded review observations

Inspected queue counts/tails and cancellation paths, paced writes, reconnect
reset paths, sorted roster updates and the allocation cleanup in view creation,
history resizing, complete send-plan construction and roster growth. No other
concrete defect was confirmed in that bounded inspection. This statement is
source-review scope, not an allocation-failure testing or leak-certification
claim. Existing focused local compatibility cases cover selected ordinary
queue, close, reconnect and roster behavior; the aggregate legacy test main
was not invoked by the compatibility harness.

Validation and integration notes

Normal compiler flags: -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -g -O2
-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2 -fstack-protector-strong.
Sanitizer compiler flags: -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -g -O1
-fno-omit-frame-pointer -fsanitize=address,undefined.
ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:halt_on_error=1
UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=1
LeakSanitizer is unavailable in this environment; no leak scan is claimed.

Each results entry records exact argv/commands, working directory, environment
overrides, return codes, captured output, source hashes, source snapshots and
binary hash. validate.py is the reproducible runner. owned-file-hashes.json
records the final mirrored owned files including the root agent's .27/.28
version macros. The earlier owned hashes are preserved separately.
app.c.diff and app.h.diff record the production changes against onekey baseline.
The Makefile integration and version bump are coordinated with the root agent.
No source documentation, transport, credential, frontend, local notice text or
terminal-signal default was modified by this state task.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Keep exact commands, return codes, output and source hashes for state tests."""
import hashlib
import fcntl
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shlex
import subprocess
import sys

EVIDENCE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
RESULTS = EVIDENCE / "results.json"


def digest(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def main():
    label, source, test, mode, *case_args = sys.argv[1:]
    root = Path(source).resolve()
    test = Path(test).resolve()
    binary = EVIDENCE / (label + ".bin")
    flags = ["-std=c11", "-Wall", "-Wextra", "-Wpedantic", "-Werror", "-g"]
    if mode == "sanitize":
        flags += ["-O1", "-fno-omit-frame-pointer", "-fsanitize=address,undefined"]
    else:
        flags += ["-O2", "-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2", "-fstack-protector-strong"]
    inputs = [test, root / "tests/test_app.c", root / "src/app.c", root / "src/app.h",
              root / "src/autocommands.c", root / "src/sim.c", root / "src/protocol.c"]
    snapshots = EVIDENCE / "source-snapshots"
    snapshots.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    source_hashes = {str(p): digest(p) for p in inputs}
    source_snapshots = {}
    for p in inputs:
        snapshot = snapshots / (source_hashes[str(p)] + "-" + p.name)
        if not snapshot.exists():
            snapshot.write_bytes(p.read_bytes())
        source_snapshots[str(p)] = str(snapshot)
    compile_cmd = ["cc"] + flags + ["-I" + str(root / "src"), "-I" + str(root / "tests"),
        "-o", str(binary), str(test), str(root / "src/app.c"),
        str(root / "src/autocommands.c"), str(root / "src/sim.c"), str(root / "src/protocol.c")]
    env = os.environ.copy()
    overrides = {}
    if mode == "sanitize":
        overrides = {"ASAN_OPTIONS": "detect_leaks=0:halt_on_error=1", "UBSAN_OPTIONS": "halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=1"}
        env.update(overrides)
    records = []
    run_commands = [("run-" + case, [str(binary), case]) for case in case_args[1:]] if case_args[:1] == ["--cases"] else [("run", [str(binary)] + case_args)]
    for phase, command in [("compile", compile_cmd)] + run_commands:
        completed = subprocess.run(command, cwd=root, env=env, text=True,
                                   stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
        log = EVIDENCE / (label + "-" + phase + ".log")
        log.write_text(completed.stdout)
        records.append({"phase": phase, "argv": command, "command": shlex.join(command),
            "cwd": str(root), "environment_overrides": overrides,
            "returncode": completed.returncode, "output_log": str(log), "output": completed.stdout})
        print(label, phase, "returncode=" + str(completed.returncode))
        if completed.stdout:
            print(completed.stdout)
        if completed.returncode and phase == "compile":
            break
    result = {"label": label, "mode": mode, "source_root": str(root),
        "source_sha256": source_hashes, "source_snapshots": source_snapshots,
        "source_changed_during_validation": [str(p) for p in inputs if digest(p) != source_hashes[str(p)]],
        "binary_sha256": digest(binary) if binary.exists() else None,
        "leak_scanning": "disabled; LeakSanitizer unavailable in this environment", "steps": records}
    with (EVIDENCE / "results.lock").open("w") as lock:
        fcntl.flock(lock, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        all_results = json.loads(RESULTS.read_text()) if RESULTS.exists() else []
        all_results.append(result)
        RESULTS.write_text(json.dumps(all_results, indent=2) + "\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
